info.name: EEBUS-Hub
info.description:
Generated from api/eebus-hub.yaml by utils/generate_postman.py — do not edit by hand, run `make postman` instead.

Set the `baseUrl` collection variable to reach a different Hub. Query parameters and header parameters are present but disabled; enable the ones a call needs.

API version 3.1.0.

item.name: SIM
List EEBUS-capable devices discovered on the network via mDNS

request.description:
Returns every SHIP-capable device the mDNS scanner currently sees on the network (only entries advertising a valid 40-character SKI are kept), sorted by name. Use this to find the SKI of a real device before trusting it — see `POST /hems/trust` (and the per-entity trust endpoints) for the pairing step that follows discovery.

By default this hub's own simulated entities are suppressed from the list (matched by a "Coretech-Innovations" brand marker) so they don't clutter discovery of real devices; start the hub with `--mdnsnosuppres` to include them too.

Requires: none.

item.name: Get simulation run state, speed factor, and elapsed time

request.description:
Reports whether the simulation is currently running, its configured speed factor, and how much simulated time has elapsed since it was last started.

Requires: none — safe to call regardless of simulation state.

item.name: Start, stop, reset, or configuration-reset the simulation

header.description: Internal token used by test automation to authorize simulation control while a compliance test run is active. Must match the server's EEBUS_HUB_INTERNAL_TEST_TOKEN environment variable; if that variable is unset, no token can bypass the block.

request.description:
Drives the simulation engine's lifecycle. Use `start` to begin ticking the simulation at a given speed, `stop` to pause it, `reset` to tear down every simulated entity and rebuild a fresh default HEMS, or `cfgreset` to restore every existing entity to its initial configuration without deleting anything.

Requires: preconditions differ per action — see the `action` enum below. While a compliance test run is active (`/testing`), all four actions are blocked with 409 unless the request carries a valid `X-EEBUS-Internal-Test-Token` header.

item.name: Get the OPEV/OSCEV EV limit log

request.description:
Returns every OPEV and OSCEV limit exchange recorded so far, in insertion order. Each exchange is one entry, carrying the EV's accept/reject outcome. The buffer holds at most 1000 entries; once full, the oldest is dropped as a new one arrives.

Requires: none — safe to call regardless of simulation state. Cleared by `DELETE /sim/EVLimitLogs` and automatically by `POST /sim` action=reset.

item.name: Clear the OPEV/OSCEV EV limit log

request.description:
Empties the EV limit log buffer and resets the per-entity bookkeeping that decides what gets logged: the CEM's record of previously sent OPEV limits and each simulated EV's record of previously logged limits. Clearing only the buffer without this bookkeeping would leave the first limit written after the clear looking like an unchanged duplicate and suppress it from the fresh log.

Requires: none.

item.name: Export the EV limit log to CSV

request.description:
Exports the EV limit log as CSV, sorted by timestamp. Any query parameter below filters the export; passing no parameters exports everything.

Requires: none.

item.name: Export the LPC/LPP load-control-limit log to CSV

query.description: Exact limit value, in the limit's own unit (A for APCL/FSCAPL, W for APPL/FSPAPL).

request.description:
Exports the LP log (see `GET /sim/LPView`) as a CSV download, sorted by timestamp. Any query parameter below filters the export by exact match; passing none exports everything currently buffered.

Requires: none.

item.name: Export the MGCP measurement log to CSV

request.description:
Exports the MGCP log (see `GET /sim/MGCPLogs`) as a CSV download, one row per snapshot, in the order the entries were recorded. No filtering is supported; the export always contains everything currently buffered. Cells for scenario fields absent from a given notify are left empty.

Requires: none.

item.name: Export the MPC measurement log to CSV

request.description:
Exports the MPC log (see `GET /sim/MPCLogs`) as a CSV download, one row per snapshot, in the order the entries were recorded. No filtering is supported; the export always contains everything currently buffered.

Requires: none.

item.name: Get the LPC/LPP load-control-limit log

request.description:
Returns every load-control-limit write exchanged for the LPC (Limitation of Power Consumption) and LPP (Limitation of Power Production) use cases, in insertion order — both regular limits (`APCL`/`APPL`) and failsafe limits (`FSCAPL`/`FSPAPL`) written by the CEM (HEMS) or a ControlBox to a controllable system (EVSE/Inverter/HeatPump). An entry appears whenever such a limit is written or its state changes (Applied → Accepted/Rejected). The buffer holds at most 1000 entries; once full, the oldest is dropped as a new one arrives.

Requires: none — safe to call regardless of simulation state. Cleared by `DELETE /sim/LPView` and automatically by `POST /sim` action=reset.

item.name: Clear the LPC/LPP load-control-limit log

request.description:
Empties the LP log buffer (see `GET /sim/LPView`).

Requires: none.

item.name: Get the MGCP measurement log

request.description:
Returns every consolidated MGCP (Monitoring of Grid Connection Point) measurement snapshot the CEM (MA) has received from any GCP, in insertion order. One entry is appended per SPINE notify; a notify may populate any subset of the scenario fields (power, energy, current, voltage, frequency), and includes [MGCP-003] value-state rejections. The buffer holds at most 1000 entries; once full, the oldest is dropped as a new one arrives.

Requires: none — safe to call regardless of simulation state. Cleared by `DELETE /sim/MGCPLogs` and automatically by `POST /sim` action=reset.

item.name: Clear the MGCP measurement log

request.description:
Empties the MGCP log buffer (see `GET /sim/MGCPLogs`).

Requires: none.

item.name: Get the MPC measurement log

request.description:
Returns every MPC (Monitoring of Power Consumption) measurement snapshot recorded so far, in insertion order. An entry is appended whenever a controllable system (EVSE/Inverter/HeatPump) or the CEM/ControlBox publishes a new measurement notify (power, current, voltage, energy, or frequency) to its MPC handler. The buffer holds at most 1000 entries; once full, the oldest is dropped as a new one arrives.

Requires: none — safe to call regardless of simulation state. Cleared by `DELETE /sim/MPCLogs` and automatically by `POST /sim` action=reset.

item.name: Clear the MPC measurement log

request.description:
Empties the MPC log buffer (see `GET /sim/MPCLogs`).

Requires: none.

item.name: Get the (deprecated) TCP trace server status

request.description:
Deprecated: the legacy TCP-12345 EEBusTracer surface was removed. This endpoint is a stub kept for backward compatibility; it always reports `enabled: false` and `port: ""`. Use `/api/v1/analyzer/stream` (SSE) for live SHIP/SPINE traffic instead.

Requires: none.

item.name: Configure the (deprecated) TCP trace server

request.description:
Deprecated: the legacy TCP-12345 EEBusTracer surface was removed. Sending `enabled: false` is accepted as a no-op and returns 200. Sending `enabled: true` always fails with 500, since the server can no longer be started; `port` is accepted but not validated or used. Use `/api/v1/analyzer/stream` (SSE) for live SHIP/SPINE traffic instead.

Requires: none.

item.name: Download the current EEBUS log file

request.description:
Downloads the EEBUS-verbosity log file the logger is currently writing to (one file per run; see `internal/logger.go`), regardless of whether file logging was explicitly started via `/sim/logs/{action}`.

Requires: the log file must exist on disk.

item.name: Get the current EEBUS log file's path

request.description:
Returns the filesystem path of the EEBUS-verbosity log file the logger is currently writing to, without downloading its contents (see `GET /sim/eebuslog` to download it).

Requires: the log file must exist on disk.

item.name: Download the saved action history as a JSON file

request.description:
Streams the saved action history (see `/sim/save`) as a downloadable JSON file (`EEBUS-Hub-export.json`), suitable for later re-loading with `POST /sim/import` on this or another hub instance.

Requires: at least one saved action; call `/sim/save` first if `GET /sim/save` reports unsaved changes.

item.name: Load a previously exported configuration file

request.description:
Uploads a JSON file previously downloaded from `GET /sim/export` and replays its create/config/patch actions to reconstruct the entities it describes, merging them into the current save history.

Requires: simulation stopped. `status: false` (still HTTP 200) means the import was rejected because at least one entity in the file would exactly duplicate an already-existing entity's configuration; no entities are created in that case.

item.name: Clear the recorded API call log

request.description:
Empties the in-memory API call log recorded by `POST /sim/log/start`, independently of whether recording is currently running.

Requires: none. Always succeeds.

item.name: Start recording every REST API call the backend receives

request.description:
Turns on the API call recorder: every subsequent request (method, URI, and JSON body for non-GET requests) is appended to an in-memory log until `POST /sim/log/stop` is called. Intended for capturing a repeatable script of API calls, distinct from the EEBUS/event file logs under `/sim/logs/*`.

Requires: API logging not already running (see `GET /sim/logState`).

item.name: Stop the API call recorder and download the recorded script

request.description:
Stops the API call recorder started by `POST /sim/log/start` and returns the recorded calls as a downloadable replay script — a `.bat` file on Windows, a `.sh` file on Linux/macOS (server OS, not client OS).

Requires: API logging currently running.

item.name: Get whether the in-memory API call recorder is running

request.description:
Reports whether the API call recorder controlled by `/sim/log/start` and `/sim/log/stop` is currently `Running` or `Stopped`. Unrelated to the file-based EEBUS/event loggers controlled by `/sim/logs/{action}`.

Requires: none.

item.name: Download the EEBUS-verbosity capture from the last logging window

request.description:
Downloads the EEBUS-verbosity portion of the in-memory buffer captured by `POST /sim/logs/{action} (action=start)` / `(action=stop)` (SHIP/SPINE trace lines).

Requires: the capture window must be stopped, and at least one EEBUS-level line must have been logged during it.

item.name: Download the Event-verbosity capture from the last logging window

request.description:
Downloads the Event-verbosity portion of the in-memory buffer captured by `POST /sim/logs/{action} (action=start)` / `(action=stop)` — the same category of entries streamed live over the `/events_ws` websocket.

Requires: the capture window must be stopped, and at least one Event-level line must have been logged during it.

item.name: Start or stop the in-memory verbosity-log capture window

variable.description: `start` begins the capture window; `stop` ends it.

request.description:
Starts or stops an in-memory capture window that buffers every log line written at any verbosity (Normal/Error/Trace/Debug/Event/EEBUS) while active, keyed by verbosity. Distinct from the always-on per-run log files under `./logs/` (see `/sim/eebuslog`) and from the API call recorder controlled by `/sim/log/*`. Starting a new window discards any previously buffered capture; once stopped, the EEBUS and Event streams captured during the window can be downloaded via `/sim/logs/eebuslogs` and `/sim/logs/eventlogs`.

Requires: none — safe to call regardless of current capture state. Calling `start` again while already capturing restarts the window and discards whatever was buffered so far; calling `stop` while already stopped is a no-op. Both still return 200.

item.name: Redo the last undone action

request.description:
Re-applies the most recently undone action (see `/sim/undo`), moving it back onto the unsaved action history.

Requires: simulation stopped (see `/sim` action=stop).

item.name: Check whether there are unsaved actions

request.description:
Reports whether every action performed so far has already been saved. `status: true` means `/sim/save` has nothing new to do (no pending actions); `status: false` means there are unsaved changes.

Requires: none.

item.name: Save all unsaved actions and clear the redo history

request.description:
Moves every action recorded since the last save (creates, config changes, patches) into the persistent save history that `GET /sim/export` reads from, collapsing repeated patches on the same entity down to their latest value. This also clears the redo history built up by `/sim/undo`, so any undone-but-not-redone actions are discarded.

Requires: none. Always succeeds; there is nothing to fail on.

item.name: Change the simulated-time-per-real-second speed factor

request.description:
Sets how many seconds of simulated time elapse per real second while the simulation is running (see `elapsedTime` in `GET /sim`). Takes effect the next time the simulation is started with `POST /sim` action=start, or immediately if the simulation is already using this value.

Requires: simulation stopped. Values below 1 are coerced up to 1; there is no configured upper bound. If the new value equals the current one, this is a no-op that still returns 200 without logging a change.

item.name: Undo the last unsaved action

request.description:
Reverts the most recently performed action that has not yet been saved (see `/sim/save`) and pushes it onto the redo stack so it can be replayed with `/sim/redo`. Performing any new action after an undo discards the redo stack.

Requires: simulation stopped (see `/sim` action=stop).

item.name: Get the current use-case availability flags

request.description:
Returns the current on/off state of all 12 use-case flags (a subset of which may be further restricted by the license — see `PATCH /sim/usecases`).

Requires: none.

item.name: Enable or disable EEBUS use cases at runtime

request.description:
Toggles which EEBUS use case handlers the CEM (HEMS) and, for MGCP, the ControlBox advertise and respond to. Only the flags present in the request body are changed; omitted flags are left as-is. Use this before creating any EVSE/EV/Inverter/Uncontrollable-device entity to decide which use cases a scenario will exercise.

Requires: simulation stopped, and no EV/EVSE/Inverter/Uncontrollable-device entity created yet (use `POST /sim` action=reset first if any exist). Every flag is additionally constrained by the current license — enabling a use case the license does not grant is rejected with 403. Flags are re-read from the license automatically on `POST /sim` action=reset.

Dependency, applied silently to the request body before anything is stored: both OPEV and OSCEV build on EVSECC, so disabling `evseccEnabled` forces `opevEnabled` AND `oscevEnabled` off, and enabling either `opevEnabled` or `oscevEnabled` forces `evseccEnabled` on. These coercions are not reported — the call returns 200 and a later `GET /sim/usecases` is the only way to observe the resulting state, which may differ from what was sent.

item.description: Simulation engine lifecycle, use-case toggles, logging, and monitoring log exports.

item.name: EV
Create a simulated EV

request.description:
Creates a new simulated EV entity, unconnected to any EVSE (connect it afterwards with POST /ev/{evId}/evse/{evseId}). No field validation is performed on the device/identification data — a malformed or empty body is accepted with each field defaulting to its Go zero value. Requires: the simulation must not be running (400 otherwise).

`opevEnabled`, `evsocEnabled` and `oscevEnabled` in the request body are overridden by the server from the currently configured license/use-case toggles before the entity is created — the values you submit for these three flags are ignored.

item.name: List all simulated EVs

request.description: Returns every simulated EV entity with its full configuration, plus whether it is currently connected to an EVSE and, if so, that EVSE's engine ID.

item.name: Get load-control limits, current draw and charge status for every EV

request.description: Convenience aggregate over every simulated EV: for each, the OPEV load-control limit data (null if the EV is not connected to an EVSE or OPEV is unavailable — the underlying error is discarded), the live per-phase current draw, and the battery charge status.

item.name: Get aggregated EV view data

request.description: Merges every simulated EV with every remote EV the HEMS has discovered into one deduplicated, deterministically sorted list — a remote entry whose SPINE entity address matches a simulated EV is dropped in favor of the simulated one. Each entry's `availableSections.oscev`/`opev` reflect whether those use cases are currently licensed; the charging/measurements sections are always present for simulated EVs.

item.name: Get one EV's configuration

request.description: Returns the given EV's full configuration merged with its live connection state (`evId`, `connectedToEVSE`, and `evseId` when connected). Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Update an EV's configuration

request.description:
Applies a partial update to the EV's static configuration (device data, current limits, battery, OSCEV device configuration, etc.). The request body is merged onto the existing config field-by-field — only JSON keys actually present in the body overwrite the corresponding field; omitted keys keep their current value. If the merged result is identical to the current configuration, the entity is left untouched (still returns 200 with changes/new/old).

OSCEV fields carry extra validation, applied only when the corresponding key is present in the request body:
- `oscevPVChargeMode` must be one of `off` / `surplusOnly` / `surplusWithThreshold`; `surplusWithThreshold` is rejected unless the EV's `oscevSurplusWithThresholdSupported` is already `true`.
- `oscevSurplusWithThresholdSupported` is immutable after creation — a request that includes this key is always rejected with 400, regardless of the value supplied.
- `oscevSurplusThresholdInWatts`, `oscevStartDelayInSeconds` and `oscevStopDelayInSeconds` must be non-negative when present.
- If threshold support is disabled, `oscevSurplusThresholdInWatts` may not be set and `oscevPVChargeMode` may not be `surplusWithThreshold` (enforced both when the fields are freshly submitted and against the EV's existing stored configuration).

item.name: Delete a simulated EV

header.description: Internal token used by test automation to bypass the active-test-run block.

request.description: Removes the EV entity. If it is currently connected to an EVSE it is disconnected first (equivalent to DELETE /ev/{evId}/evse/{evseId}); a disconnect failure is only logged, it does not block the deletion. Requires: the simulation must not be running, and no compliance test run may be active (unless a valid X-EEBUS-Internal-Test-Token is supplied).

item.name: Get the EV's permitted electrical connection value

request.description: Returns the OPEV/EVCC electrical-connection permitted value and range for phase A, as a single-element array. Requires: the EV must be connected to an EVSE, with both its OPEV and EVCC handlers running (400 otherwise).

item.name: Set the EV's permitted electrical connection values

request.description: Writes the OPEV/EVCC electrical-connection permitted value and range for all three phases. The request body must contain exactly 3 entries, in phase A, B, C order — fewer than 3 entries causes the request to fail (the handler indexes elements 0/1/2 directly). Requires the EV's OPEV and EVCC handlers to be running (400 otherwise). Unlike the GET on this path, which returns only phase A, the PATCH always writes all three phases.

item.name: Get the HEMS operating state as seen by this EV

request.description: Reads the DeviceDiagnosisStateData the CEM/HEMS last reported over the OPEV connection — the HEMS's own operating state and last error code, from this EV's point of view. Requires: the EV must be connected to an EVSE, a CEM entity must be visible on that EVSE's paired device, and the EV's OPEV handler must be running (400/500 otherwise — see responses).

item.name: Get the last OPEV heartbeat received from the HEMS

request.description: Reads the DeviceDiagnosisHeartbeatData last received from the CEM/HEMS over the OPEV connection. Requires: the EV must be connected to an EVSE, a CEM entity must be visible on that EVSE's paired device, and the EV's OPEV handler must be running (400/500 otherwise — see responses).

item.name: Get the EV's OPEV load-control limits

request.description: Returns the raw SPINE LoadControlLimitListData the EV currently holds for the OPEV use case, as exactly 3 entries in phase A, B, C order (the phase is implied by array position, not carried in the payload). Requires: the EV must be connected to an EVSE (400 otherwise), and the OPEV handler must be running (400 if OPEV is disabled for this EV).

item.name: Get the EV's live current draw

request.description: Returns the EV's current instantaneous per-phase current draw in Amps, as reported by the simulation (or the pinned testing-mode values, if the EV is in testing mode). Does not require the EV to be connected to an EVSE: the simulation tick still runs while unconnected, so if the EV's `dischargingEnable` is true it keeps discharging (non-zero current) even without an EVSE; otherwise its charging state is NotCharging and current decays toward 0 A rather than dropping to it instantly.

item.name: Get the EV's battery charge status

request.description: Returns the EV's simulated battery state: charging state, state of charge as a percentage of effective (health-derated) capacity, current charge and nominal capacity in kWh, and battery health as a percentage.

item.name: Plug an EV into an EVSE

request.description: Simulates plugging the EV's cable into the EVSE: registers the EV with the EVSE (fails with 400 if the EV is already connected to any EVSE, or if the EVSE ID does not resolve to an EVSE entity). If the target EVSE already has a local SKI — i.e. it has already been started via POST /evse/{evseId}/trust or was already running — the EV's own EEBUS service (EVCC/EVEM and, if enabled, OPEV/OSCEV/EVSOC handlers) is started immediately as part of this call; otherwise the EV's service starts later, when the EVSE is trusted. An EV can be connected to at most one EVSE at a time; use DELETE on this path first to move it to a different EVSE. An EV plugged into an EVSE in testing mode enters testing mode too, pinned at 0 W, and returns to simulation mode when it is unplugged or the EVSE leaves testing mode, unless PATCH /ev/{evId}/mode sets testing mode on it in between.

item.name: Unplug an EV from its EVSE

request.description: Simulates unplugging the EV: removes it from the EVSE's connected-EV list and tears down the EV's EEBUS service (EVCC/EVEM and any running OPEV/OSCEV/EVSOC handlers unsubscribe from SPINE events). Returns 400 if the EV is not currently connected to any EVSE. The evseId path parameter must resolve to an existing EVSE entity, but the EV is disconnected from whichever EVSE it is actually attached to — it need not be the one named in the path. An EV in testing mode because of its EVSE returns to simulation mode; one put into testing mode through PATCH /ev/{evId}/mode stays in it.

item.name: Get Image

request.description: Returns the EV's stored Base64-encoded image. Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Upload Image

request.description: Stores a Base64-encoded image for the given EV (used by UIs for device branding). Overwrites any previously stored image unconditionally; no format/size validation is performed. Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Delete Image

request.description: Clears the EV's stored image. When there is no saved image the call is a 404 and nothing is written; otherwise the image is cleared and the call is a 200.

item.name: Get the EV simulation/testing mode and pinned values

request.description: mode is "simulation" (default, values driven by the hub's charging model) or "testing" (values pinned to whatever was last set via PATCH /ev/{evId}/values). live always reports the currently effective readings, whichever mode is active.

item.name: Toggle the EV simulation/testing mode

request.description: Switches the EV between simulation and testing mode. The pinned override values are set separately via PATCH /ev/{evId}/values. While the EV's EVSE is in testing mode the EV must stay in it: testingMode false is rejected with 409 (see lockedByParent in the response). An EV put into testing mode by this endpoint stays in it when its EVSE leaves testing mode and when it is unplugged. This includes an EV that was already in testing mode because of its EVSE: testingMode true makes that testing mode the EV's own.

item.name: Get EV OPEV state

request.description: Returns the OPEV per-phase load-control limits the EV is currently operating under, together with the OPEV connection, heartbeat and controller operating state. Limits are read from the EV's live SPINE LoadControl feature.

item.name: Get EV OSCEV state

request.description: Returns the OSCEV PV-charge configuration (mode, surplus threshold, start/stop delays) together with the current-consumption/power recommendation the EV is acting on, its OSCEV connection heartbeat and controller operating state. Requires the OSCEV use case to be licensed (403 otherwise).

item.name: Update EV OSCEV configuration

request.description:
Updates the EV's own OSCEV PV-charge configuration (as opposed to PATCH /ev/{evId}, which can also set these same fields as part of a broader config update — both paths converge on the same underlying state). Requires the OSCEV use case to be licensed (403 otherwise). Validation, applied per field only when present in the body:
- `pvChargeMode` must be one of `off` / `surplusOnly` / `surplusWithThreshold`; `surplusWithThreshold` is rejected unless the EV currently supports threshold mode (surplusWithThresholdSupported).
- `surplusThresholdInWatts` must be non-negative, and may not be set at all when threshold support is disabled.
- `startDelayInSeconds` and `stopDelayInSeconds` must be non-negative.

item.name: Set the EV forced measurement values (testing mode only)

request.description: Pins the EV's reported charging power/current/SoC verbatim. Requires testing mode (400 otherwise). Every field optional; omitted fields keep their value.

item.description: Simulated electric vehicle entities and their charging/measurement data.

item.name: EVSE
Create a simulated EVSE

request.description:
Creates a new simulated EVSE entity. The EVSE's own EEBUS service is not started yet — it starts lazily on the first POST /evse/{evseId}/trust call. Requires: the simulation must not be running (400 otherwise).

Validates deviceName/brandName/deviceCode/serialNumber/vendor.code/ vendor.name (all required, non-empty), failsafeValue/failsafeDuration/ failSafeDurationMax and nominalPower/nominalCurrent bounds (see EVSEConfig field descriptions), and device-name/device-address uniqueness against every existing EVSE. On success, `evseccEnabled`, `lpcEnabled` and `mpcEnabled` are overridden from the currently configured license/use-case toggles, `brandName` is fixed to "Coretech-Innovations", and `contractualPowerMax` is cleared — see EVSEConfig for details. An optional `trustConnections` array records mutual-trust peers to be established when the simulation starts.

item.name: Add an external (real) EVSE for pairing

request.description: Registers a real, non-simulated EVSE by SKI so it can be discovered/paired via mDNS, alongside simulated EVSEs. Requires: the simulation must not be running. remoteSki is normalized (colons/case) before being stored; a request without a usable SKI is rejected.

item.name: List all simulated EVSEs

request.description: Returns every simulated EVSE entity with its full configuration, pairing state and live LPC status.

item.name: Get EVSE details by ID

request.description: Reports the EVSE's own SKI (`ski`) alongside the SKI it currently observes as its connected controller (`remoteSki`) and whether that connection is live (`connectedToHEMS`). This is the read side of SKI-trust corroboration: after registering a remote SKI via POST /evse/{evseId}/trust (and the matching trust on the controller's own side), call this endpoint to confirm the pairing actually took by checking that `remoteSki` matches the expected controller SKI. `remoteSki`/`connectedToHEMS` are populated at the SHIP transport level, so they reflect any connected controller regardless of which use cases (e.g. EVSECC) are enabled. Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Update an EVSE's configuration

request.description: Applies a partial update to the EVSE's configuration. The request body is merged onto the existing config field-by-field — only JSON keys present in the body overwrite the corresponding field; omitted keys keep their current value. If the merged result is identical to the current configuration, the entity is left untouched (still returns 200 with changes/new/old). The same validation and uniqueness checks as POST /evse/add apply (see EVSEConfig field descriptions); brandName and contractualPowerMax cannot be changed through this endpoint, and trustConnections is not honored here (add-only).

item.name: Delete a simulated EVSE

header.description: Internal token used by test automation to bypass the active-test-run block.

request.description: Removes the EVSE entity. Any EV currently connected to it is disconnected first (equivalent to DELETE /ev/{evId}/evse/{evseId} for each); a disconnect failure is only logged, it does not block the deletion. Requires: the simulation must not be running, and no compliance test run may be active (unless a valid X-EEBUS-Internal-Test-Token is supplied).

item.name: Get the EVSE's MPC electrical measurements

request.description: Returns the EVSE's current total/per-phase power, energy, current, voltage and frequency, mapped into the MPC measurement shape (see MPCMeasurements). Does not require MPC to be enabled — it always returns whatever the EVSE's live simulated/testing-mode readings are (fields the EVSE has no data for are simply omitted).

item.name: Manually inject electrical measurements into the EVSE

request.description:
Overwrites the EVSE's electrical measurements (power/current/voltage per phase, energy, frequency) for simulation/testing purposes, bypassing normal use-case computation. Requires: the simulation must be running, and no EV may currently be connected to this EVSE — if one is connected, the request is rejected so manual measurements cannot fight the EV's own charging behaviour. Only fields present in the request body are changed; omitted fields keep their current value.

Known quirk: injected values are written into the SPINE MPC local data (visible to a paired HEMS via GET /hems/MpcMeasurementData) but are NOT reflected back on the sibling GET /evse/{evseId}/electricalMeasurements — the code path that would sync them back (`h.measurements = measurements`) is commented out. Use GET /hems/MpcMeasurementData to verify an injected value took effect, not this endpoint's own GET.

item.name: Get the EVSE's error state

request.description: Reads the EVSECC DeviceDiagnosisStateData currently held by the EVSE. Requires: the EVSECC use case must be licensed (checked once globally, not per EVSE) — 400 otherwise. Note: unlike the sibling POST/DELETE on this path (which return 404 when evseId does not resolve to an EVSE entity), this GET returns 400 for that case.

item.name: Force the EVSE into an error state

request.description: Testing aid that drives the EVSE's EVSECC DeviceDiagnosisStateData into a failure condition. The device is always driven to operatingState "failure" regardless of what (if anything) is submitted for operatingState — only lastErrorCode is actually applied (see the ErrorState schema). While in this state, ApproveOrChangeLimits zeroes out the current limits offered to any connected EV, effectively stopping its charging — this does not change the LPC controllable-system's CSState. Requires: the EVSECC use case must be licensed (checked once globally, not per EVSE) — 400 otherwise.

item.name: Clear the EVSE's error state

request.description: Restores the EVSECC DeviceDiagnosisStateData to operatingState "normalOperation" with lastErrorCode "0". Requires: the EVSECC use case must be licensed (checked once globally, not per EVSE) — 400 otherwise.

item.name: Force the EVSE controllable-system state (testing aid)

request.description:
Inject the EVSE's LPC controllable system into a chosen state once, so a tester can start a scenario with the device already in that state. The real state machine resumes on the next tick — incoming limit writes are processed and transitions out of the forced state follow the normal FSM. See CSState for what each of the five states means.

Requires: the EVSE must have a controllable system (LPC enabled), AND the EVSE must already be in testing mode (PATCH /evse/{evseId}/mode with testingMode=true) — both are checked, and either missing returns 400. This is a one-shot injection: it is applied on the next simulate tick and is not re-applied afterwards.

item.name: Get the EVSE's display image

request.description: Returns the EVSE's stored Base64-encoded image. Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Upload the EVSE's display image

request.description: Stores a base64-encoded image for the EVSE, replacing any previous one.

item.name: Delete the EVSE's display image

request.description: Clears the stored image. When no image is currently stored the call is a 400 and nothing is written; otherwise the image is cleared and the call is a 200.

item.name: Get the latest LPC heartbeat received from the CEM

request.description: Returns the last DeviceDiagnosisHeartbeatData the EVSE received from its CEM peer over LPC. Requires: the EVSE must have a controllable system (LPC enabled) — 400 if LPC is disabled.

item.name: Get the latest LPC heartbeat sent by the EVSE

request.description: Returns the last DeviceDiagnosisHeartbeatData the EVSE sent to its CEM peer over LPC. Requires: the EVSE must have a controllable system (LPC enabled) — 400 if LPC is disabled.

item.name: Get the active power consumption limit applied to the EVSE

request.description: Returns the LPC Active Power Consumption Limit (APCL) currently reported by the EVSE. Requires: the EVSE must have a controllable system (LPC enabled) — 400 if LPC is disabled.

item.name: Get the EVSE's LPC controllable-system state

request.description: Returns the EVSE's LPC controllable-system FSM state. currentState is the empty string if the EVSE has no controllable system (LPC disabled) — this is not an error. See CSState for the meaning of each value.

item.name: Get the EVSE's configured failsafe power limit and duration

request.description: Returns the EVSE's configured failsafeValue (W) and failsafeDuration (converted here to seconds) — the limit the EVSE falls back to in the Failsafe controllable-system state. Unlike the other lpc* GET endpoints, this always succeeds (it reads static configuration, not live LPC state) — it does not require LPC to be enabled.

item.name: Get the EVSE's LPC power constraints

request.description: Returns the LPC power-consumption constraints (nominal and contractual maxima) the EVSE reports. Requires: the EVSE must have a controllable system (LPC enabled) — 400 if LPC is disabled.

item.name: Get the EVSE's manufacturer/device identification

request.description: Reads the EVSECC DeviceClassificationManufacturerData from the EVSE's own local SPINE data. Requires: the EVSECC use case must be licensed (checked once globally against the license, not per EVSE) — 400 otherwise.

item.name: Get the EVSE simulation/testing mode and pinned power

request.description: currentState in the response is the EVSE's live LPC controllable-system state (empty string if the EVSE has no controllable system) — see CSState for the meaning of each value. It is independent of simulation/testing mode: forcing testing mode does not change or bypass the LPC FSM (use POST /evse/{evseId}/forceState for that).

item.name: Toggle the EVSE simulation/testing mode

request.description: Switches the EVSE between simulation and testing mode. The pinned override values are set separately via PATCH /evse/{evseId}/values. Entering testing mode seeds the pinned total power from the EVSE's current simulated load, so the first GET after enabling it reflects continuity rather than a jump to zero. This is a prerequisite for POST /evse/{evseId}/forceState, which additionally requires testing mode to be active. Enabling also puts every connected EV that is not yet in testing mode into it (each pinned at its current power), and an EV connected later enters it pinned at 0 W; while the EVSE stays in testing mode its EVs cannot leave it. Disabling returns the EVs that are in testing mode because of the EVSE to simulation mode; an EV put into testing mode through PATCH /ev/{evId}/mode stays in it.

item.name: Get SHIP QR-pairing data for the EVSE

request.description: Returns the SHIP QR-code pairing text for the EVSE's own EEBUS service. Requires: the EVSE's service must already be running (started via POST /evse/{evseId}/trust or otherwise) — 400 if it has not started yet. Note: a malformed evseId, and evseId resolving to a non-EVSE entity, both return 400 here; 404 is reserved for an evseId that resolves to no entity at all (same split as GET /evse/{evseId}/errorState).

item.name: Get remote devices connected to this EVSE

request.description: Returns the SPINE devices currently connected/paired to this EVSE, with each device's address, supported use cases and exposed feature types.

item.name: Trust the HEMS/CEM from the EVSE side

request.description:
Registers the given remote SKI as trusted for pairing on this EVSE. If the EVSE has not started its EEBUS service yet (no local SKI), it is started first as part of this call, and every EV already connected to it (whose own EEBUS service has not started) is started as well. Requires: the simulation must not be in the brief transitional "stopping" window after `POST /sim` `action: stop` (`Engine.isAllowedToPairDevices` — despite its name this is **not** "the simulation must be running": it also returns true while the simulation has never been started, or is fully stopped; only the few seconds while a Stop() teardown is in flight return false). 400 "Simulation not running" otherwise (the error message is misleading given the actual condition). This is one half of mutual trust; the HEMS side must also trust this EVSE's SKI via POST /hems/trust for pairing to complete.

The request body field is named `remoteSki` (lowercase "ki") on the server's binding struct; Go's JSON decoder matches field names case-insensitively when there is no exact match, so `remoteSKI` (as documented below) is also accepted in practice. The value is normalized (colons/case) before use; an empty or all-whitespace SKI is rejected.

item.name: Untrust a remote device from the EVSE

request.description: Removes the given remote SKI from the EVSE's trusted-peer list. Unlike the POST on this path, this does not require the simulation to be running. Same field-name note as POST applies: the body is bound to a `remoteSki` field, matched case-insensitively.

item.name: Set the EVSE forced measurement values (testing mode only)

request.description: Pins the EVSE's reported total power, and optionally per-phase power/current/voltage/frequency, verbatim. Requires testing mode (set via PATCH /evse/{evseId}/mode first) — 400 otherwise. Every field is optional; an omitted field keeps its current pinned/simulated value.

item.name: Get all external (real) EVSEs

request.description: Returns every real EVSE registered via POST /evse/addExt. Returns an empty array when none are registered.

item.name: Modify an external (real) EVSE

request.description: Updates an existing external EVSE entry's remoteSki/deviceName/imgBase64. Requires: at least one external EVSE must already be registered, and evseId must match an existing entry. Changing remoteSki is rejected while the simulation is running.

item.name: Remove an external (real) EVSE

header.description: Internal token used by test automation to bypass the active-test-run block.

request.description: Removes a registered external EVSE entry. Requires: the simulation must not be running, and no compliance test run may be active (unless a valid X-EEBUS-Internal-Test-Token is supplied).

item.description: Simulated EV supply equipment (charging stations) acting as LPC controllable systems.

item.name: HEMS
Get the current HEMS configuration and state

request.description: Returns the HEMS configuration together with its live SKI and the energy meter's current fuse limit. `config.lpcState`/`config.lppState` are refreshed from the LPC/LPP controllable-system state machines just before the response is built, and `config.oscevHeartbeatActive` reflects the live OSCEV heartbeat status — these three fields are always current, unlike the rest of `config` which is the stored configuration. Returns an empty array `[]` (not a 404) when no HEMS has been added yet.

item.name: Update the HEMS configuration

request.description:
Partially updates the stored HEMS configuration. The request body is decoded on top of the current configuration, so omitted fields keep their existing value.

While the simulation is RUNNING, only `imgBase64` may be changed (any other field difference is ignored for that request); this is the one case where a PATCH is accepted while running. If `imgBase64` is unchanged and the simulation is running, the request fails with 400.

While the simulation is STOPPED, the following fields are validated and applied individually (a field is only applied if its new value differs from the current one AND passes its check below); at least one field must actually change or the response is 400 ("Invalid request body"):
- `fuseLimit` (Amperes) — applied via the same path as `PATCH
  /hems/config/FuseCurrentLimit` when >= 0.

- `quantaTime` (seconds) — applied when >= 1.
- `stepUpdateDuration` (seconds) — applied when >= 1.
- `currentIncrementalStep` (Amperes) — applied when > 0.
- `fuseSafetyMargin` (percent) — applied when >= 10.
- `powerTransferDelay` (seconds) — applied when >= 1.
- `algorithm` — applied when it is `FirstComeFirstServe` or `RoundRobin`;
  any other value is silently ignored (not an error).

- `lpcInfo`, `lppInfo`, `failsafeDuration`, `failSafeDurationMax` and all
  other fields — applied unconditionally with no bound checking (unlike
  `POST /hems/add`, no non-zero or range validation is performed here).

The use-case availability fields and `controllableSystemEnabled` are refused by this route: submitting one with a value that differs from the current one is a 400 and applies nothing. Repeating the current value is accepted and ignored, so a body read back from `GET /hems` can be submitted unchanged. Use `PATCH /sim/usecases` to change use-case availability.

item.name: Delete the HEMS entity

request.description:
Tears down the HEMS EEBUS service, unregisters all its remote-device trust relationships and removes it from the simulation engine. If no HEMS exists this is a no-op that still returns 200 (the loop over entities simply finds nothing to delete).

Requires: simulation STOPPED. Blocked with 409 while a test run is active (see `POST /testrun`), unless the request carries a valid test-run token.

item.name: Get the Active Power Consumption Limit (APCL) reported by all connected LPC devices

request.description: Returns each connected LPC device's current APCL as an object keyed by device address (**not** an array). Devices whose APCL could not be read are omitted. See `GET /hems/LpcDevicesData` for the same data alongside failsafe values and constraints.

item.name: Send the Active Power Consumption Limit (APCL) to all connected LPC devices

request.description:
Sends an LPC load-control limit write to every remote controllable-system device (splitting `value` evenly across all connected devices when active=true and value > 0). `active` is required; `value` is additionally required when `active` is true (400 "Data missing" otherwise). See `lpcAPCL` for the durationSeconds/durationIndefinite precedence rule.

`success` reflects whether *all* targeted devices accepted the write — see `APCLDataSuccessResponse` for the exact semantics, including the vacuous-success case when no LPC devices are connected. See `GET /hems/LpcDevicesData` to discover connected devices' addresses and current APCL state.

item.name: Send the Active Power Consumption Limit (APCL) to all connected LPC devices (partial)

request.description: Behaves like `POST /hems/ActivePowerConsumptionLimit`, except `active` is not required — the raw body is forwarded as-is (any subset of fields). Still returns 400 for a malformed JSON body.

request.description:

item.name: Get the Active Power Production Limit (APPL) reported by all connected LPP devices

request.description: Returns each connected LPP device's current APPL as an object keyed by device address (**not** an array). Devices whose APPL could not be read are omitted. Requires the LPP use case to be licensed/enabled (400 otherwise).

item.name: Send the Active Power Production Limit (APPL) to all connected LPP devices

request.description:
Sends an LPP load-control limit write to every remote controllable-system device (splitting `value` evenly across all connected devices when active=true and value < 0). Production limit values are negative numbers (the magnitude of power that must not be exceeded while producing). `active` is required; `value` is additionally required when `active` is true (400 "Data missing" otherwise). See `lppAPPL` for the durationSeconds/durationIndefinite precedence rule.

`success` reflects whether *all* targeted devices accepted the write — see `APPLDataSuccessResponse` for the exact semantics, including the vacuous-success case when no LPP devices are connected. See `GET /hems/LppDevicesData` to discover connected devices' addresses and current APPL state.

request.description:

Requires: the LPP use case must be licensed/enabled, and the device must be paired and exposing the LPP controllable-system role.

request.description:

item.name: Get the LPP power constraints reported by all connected devices

request.description: Returns each connected LPP device's nominal/contractual power production constraints as an object keyed by device address (**not** an array). Devices whose constraints could not be read are omitted. Requires the LPP use case to be licensed/enabled (400 otherwise).

item.name: Change a heat pump's OHPCF PowerSequence state

request.description: Writes state to the announced PowerSequence of the heat pump at deviceAddress (`Alternatives[0].PowerSequence[0].State.State`). Requires: the heat pump has already announced an optional power-consumption process (see `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/announceOptional`) whose PowerSequence has a Description block. The hub is a testing tool: the requested state is forwarded to the device as-is with no client-side transition validation, so a tester can request a transition the OHPCF state machine would normally forbid to observe the device's reaction — the `isPausable`/`isStoppable` flags reported by `GET /hems/OhpcfMonitorData` are informational only and are not consulted before the write. The EEBUS write outcome is always reported in the 200 body via success/reason; it does not change the HTTP status.

item.name: Get the Failsafe Active Power Consumption Limit (FSCAPL) reported by all connected LPC devices

request.description: Returns each connected LPC device's current failsafe power limit/duration as an object keyed by device address (**not** an array). Devices whose FSCAPL could not be read are omitted.

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Consumption Limit (FSCAPL) to all connected LPC devices

request.description:
Sets the LPC failsafe power limit and/or minimum failsafe duration (via two separate DeviceConfiguration key writes) on every connected LPC device — the value each device falls back to if it loses the HEMS heartbeat (see `POST /hems/heartbeat`). `value` is required (400 "Data missing" if omitted); `durationSeconds` is optional. To send only a duration, use `POST /hems/FailsafeDurationForLpc` instead.

`success` reflects whether *all* targeted devices accepted the write — unlike the APCL bulk endpoint, this endpoint reports `success=false` (not true) with `reason="No entities found"` when no LPC devices are connected.

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Consumption Limit (FSCAPL) to all connected LPC devices (partial)

request.description: Behaves like `POST /hems/FailsafeActivePowerLimit`, except `value` is not required — the raw body is forwarded as-is (any subset of fields).

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Consumption Limit (FSCAPL) to one LPC device

request.description:

Requires: the device must be paired and exposing the LPC controllable-system role.

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Consumption Limit (FSCAPL) to one LPC device (partial)

request.description: Behaves like `POST .../{deviceAddress}`, except `value` is not required — the raw body is forwarded as-is (any subset of fields).
