request.description: Returns each connected LPP device's current failsafe power limit/duration as an object keyed by device address (**not** an array). Devices whose FSPAPL could not be read are omitted. Requires the LPP use case to be licensed/enabled (400 otherwise).

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Production Limit (FSPAPL) to all connected LPP devices

request.description:
Sets the LPP failsafe power limit and/or minimum failsafe duration on every connected LPP device — the value each device falls back to if it loses the HEMS heartbeat (see `POST /hems/heartbeat`). `value` is required (400 "Data missing" if omitted); `durationSeconds` is optional. To send only a duration, use `POST /hems/FailsafeDurationForLpp` instead.

`success` reflects whether *all* targeted devices accepted the write — unlike the APPL bulk endpoint, this endpoint reports `success=false` (not true) with `reason="No entities found"` when no LPP devices are connected.

Requires: the LPP use case must be licensed/enabled (400 otherwise).

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Production Limit (FSPAPL) to all connected LPP devices (partial)

request.description:
Behaves like `POST /hems/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit`, except `value` is not required — the raw body is forwarded as-is (any subset of fields).

Requires: the LPP use case must be licensed/enabled (400 otherwise).

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Production Limit (FSPAPL) to one LPP device

request.description:
Same validation and semantics as `POST /hems/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit`, targeted at a single device. `deviceAddress` is looked up among the LPP controllable-system remote entities; an unknown address returns 404.

Requires: the LPP use case must be licensed/enabled, and the device must be paired and exposing the LPP controllable-system role.

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Production Limit (FSPAPL) to one LPP device (partial)

request.description:
Behaves like `POST .../{deviceAddress}`, except `value` is not required — the raw body is forwarded as-is (any subset of fields).

Requires: the LPP use case must be licensed/enabled.

item.name: Send only the minimum failsafe duration for LPC to all connected devices

request.description: Equivalent to `POST /hems/FailsafeActivePowerLimit` but sends only `durationSeconds` (the request body is bound the same way — as an `FCAPL` — but `value` is cleared before sending, so any `value` in the request is ignored). `durationSeconds` is required (400 "Data missing" if omitted). Same vacuous-failure behavior as `POST /hems/FailsafeActivePowerLimit`: reports `success=false, reason="No entities found"` when no LPC devices are connected.

item.name: Send only the minimum failsafe duration for LPC to one device

request.description:
Equivalent to `POST /hems/FailsafeActivePowerLimit/{deviceAddress}` but sends only `durationSeconds` (`value` is cleared before sending). `durationSeconds` is required (400 "Data missing" if omitted).

Requires: the device must be paired and exposing the LPC controllable-system role.

item.name: Send only the minimum failsafe duration for LPP to all connected devices

request.description: Equivalent to `POST /hems/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit` but sends only `durationSeconds` (`value` is cleared before sending). `durationSeconds` is required (400 "Data missing" if omitted). Unlike the other LPP bulk endpoints, this one does **not** check whether the LPP use case is licensed/enabled. Same vacuous-failure behavior as `POST /hems/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit`: reports `success=false, reason="No entities found"` when no LPP devices are connected.

item.name: Send only the minimum failsafe duration for LPP to one device

request.description:
Equivalent to `POST /hems/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit/{deviceAddress}` but sends only `durationSeconds` (`value` is cleared before sending). `durationSeconds` is required (400 "Data missing" if omitted).

**Known issue:** `deviceAddress` is resolved through the LPC device registry, not the LPP one (unlike every other `/{deviceAddress}` LPP endpoint). In practice this only succeeds for an address that is also registered as an LPC controllable system; a device that supports LPP but not LPC returns 404 here even though it is a valid LPP device address elsewhere (e.g. in `GET /hems/LppDevicesData`).

item.name: Get LPC data (APCL, failsafe, constraints) for all connected devices

request.description: Returns, per connected LPC controllable-system device, its address, SKI, current APCL, current failsafe consumption limit and power-consumption constraints in one call — a convenience combining what `GET /hems/ActivePowerConsumptionLimit`, `GET /hems/FailsafeActivePowerLimit` and `GET /hems/ActivePowerLimitConstraints` return separately. Unlike those three (which return objects keyed by device address), this returns a bare array. Unlike `GET /hems/LppDevicesData` below, this endpoint does **not** gate on the LPC use case being licensed/enabled.

item.name: Get LPP data (APPL, failsafe, constraints) for all connected devices

request.description:
Returns, per connected LPP controllable-system device, its address, SKI, current APPL, current failsafe production limit and power-production constraints in one call — a convenience combining what `GET /hems/ActivePowerProductionLimit`, `GET /hems/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit` and `GET /hems/ActivePowerProductionLimitConstraints` return separately. Unlike those three (which return objects keyed by device address), this returns a bare array.

Requires: the LPP use case must be licensed/enabled (400 otherwise).

item.name: Get the latest MGCP measurement snapshot the HEMS (MA) holds

request.description: Returns a point-in-time snapshot (not history — see `GET /sim/MGCPLogs` for the append-only log) of the grid-connection-point measurements the HEMS currently holds, keyed by the HEMS's own device address so the UI Data badge attaches to the HEMS bus item. Requires: the monitored ControlBox (GCP) already added and trust-paired to this HEMS — see `POST /controlbox/add` and `POST /controlbox/trust`; the snapshot stays empty until the SPINE data-change callback that populates it has fired at least once for that device. The handler also checks the MGCP use-case-availability flag, but that flag is initialized once at startup and never left unset, so in a running server the "not enabled" branch below cannot actually be reached.

item.name: Get MPC measurement data from every connected device

request.description: Returns the latest Monitoring of Power Consumption measurement snapshot for every remote entity paired to the HEMS's MPC handler (EVSE, Inverter, HeatPump, ControlBox SubMeter and similar monitored-unit actors). Requires: a HEMS present. The handler also checks the MPC use-case-availability flag, but that flag is initialized once at startup (and only re-initialized by `POST /sim` with `action: "reset"`) and is never left unset, so in a running server the "not supported" branch below cannot actually be reached — overall license validity is still enforced globally (403 on an expired license).

item.name: Get OHPCF data for every announced heat pump

request.description: Returns the latest OHPCF (Optimization of Self Consumption by Heat Pump Compressor Flexibility) PowerSequence data for every remote Compressor entity paired to the HEMS's OHPCF handler. A heat pump is included only once it has announced an optional power-consumption process with a non-empty Alternatives/PowerSequence — see `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/announceOptional` — devices that have not (yet) announced are silently omitted, not reported with an empty entry. Requires: a HEMS present. The handler also checks the OHPCF use-case-availability flag, but that flag is initialized once at startup and never left unset, so in a running server the "not supported" branch cannot actually be reached.

item.name: Send an OHPCF start time to a heat pump

request.description: Writes a start time to the announced PowerSequence of the heat pump at deviceAddress (`Alternatives[0].PowerSequence[0].Schedule.StartTime`). Identical in every respect to `PATCH /hems/SendOhpcfStartTime/{deviceAddress}` below — both HTTP methods are wired to the same handler. Requires: the heat pump has already announced an optional power-consumption process (see `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/announceOptional`) whose PowerSequence has both a State and a Description block. The EEBUS write outcome (success or failure) is always reported in the 200 body via success/reason; it does not change the HTTP status.

item.name: Send an OHPCF start time to a heat pump

request.description: Identical to `POST /hems/SendOhpcfStartTime/{deviceAddress}` above — both HTTP methods are wired to the same handler and behave the same way, including the "already announced" requirement.

item.name: Create the HEMS (CEM) entity

request.description:
Creates the single HEMS/CEM simulation entity, starts its EEBUS service and registers the use cases enabled by the current license (LPC, LPP, MPC, MGCP, OPEV, EVSECC, EVSOC, MOI, MOB, COB, OHPCF). There can only be one HEMS at a time — a second call fails with 400 ("cem is already added"). `deviceBrand` is always overwritten to `"Coretech-Innovations"` server-side regardless of what is sent.

The body is validated before creation; any of the following makes the whole request fail with 400 (all field names below are reported together in `err` when more than one is invalid):
- `fuseSafetyMargin` must be >= 10 (percent of the fuse limit reserved as
  headroom).

- `quantaTime` must be >= 1 (seconds).
- `stepUpdateDuration` must be >= 1 (seconds).
- `currentIncrementalStep` must be > 0 (Amperes).
- `powerTransferDelay` must be >= 1 (seconds).
- `vendorCode`, `deviceModel`, `deviceBrand`, `serialNumber`, `deviceName`
  must all be non-empty.

- `lpcInfo.contractualPowerMax` must be set.
- `lpcInfo.failsafeValue` must be non-zero.
- `lppInfo.contractualPowerMax` must be set.
- `lppInfo.failsafeValue` must be non-zero.
- `failsafeDuration` must be non-zero (hours).
- `failSafeDurationMax` must be non-zero (hours).

If `lpcInfo`/`lppInfo` are omitted entirely, defaults are used (`failsafeValue: 25000` W, `failsafeDuration: 2` h, `failSafeDurationMax: 24` h, `contractualPowerMax: 25000` W, `approveWriteLimit: true`) — in that case the top-level `failsafeDuration`/`failSafeDurationMax` non-zero checks above are skipped for that CS. No upper bound (e.g. 24h) is enforced on `failsafeDuration`/`failSafeDurationMax` when they are supplied explicitly; only "non-zero" is checked.

`controllableSystemEnabled` defaults to `true` when omitted.

Requires: simulation STOPPED (`engine.IsSimulationRunning()` must be false) and a valid license.

item.name: Register a real (non-simulated) HEMS/CEM by SKI

request.description:
Records the SKI of a real HEMS/CEM so simulated actors can be paired with it (there is no simulated CEM entity created — this is metadata only, used by `GET /hemsExt` and the pairing UI). `remoteSKI` is normalized the same way as `POST /hems/trust` (whitespace stripped, lowercased) via `FormatSki`. There is only one external HEMS slot; calling this again overwrites the previous one.

Requires: simulation STOPPED.

item.name: Get the current OPEV/OSCEV distribution algorithm

request.description: Returns the currently configured distribution algorithm and, for Round Robin, its shuffle interval. **Response body is only written when the current algorithm is `RoundRobin`** — for any other value (e.g. the default `FirstComeFirstServe`, or an empty value if none was ever set) the handler writes nothing at all, so the client receives an empty 200 response with no JSON body.

item.name: Switch the OPEV/OSCEV distribution algorithm to Round Robin

request.description:
Switches the EV-current distribution algorithm used by the OPEV allocation loop (see `algorithm` on `POST /hems/add` / `PATCH /hems`). `algorithm` is matched case-insensitively, but the **only** value this endpoint currently accepts is `RoundRobin` — any other value (including `"FirstComeFirstServe"`) is rejected with 400 ("invalid Algorithm type"). There is no dedicated endpoint to switch back to FirstComeFirstServe; use `PATCH /hems` with `algorithm: FirstComeFirstServe` instead.

`quantaTime` (the round-robin shuffle interval) is required and must be >= 1 second.

Requires: simulation STOPPED.

item.name: Switch a COB device's active control mode

request.description: Selects which COB setpoint category (power or pcc) governs the paired device, by writing its "batteryActiveControlMode" device-configuration key. Requires: a device paired at deviceAddress that exposes a batteryActiveControlMode configuration key. mode must be "power" or "pcc" (case-insensitive). Unlike most COB limit routes, a failed EEBUS write is reported as HTTP 500, not 200. The handler also checks a COB use-case-availability flag, but that flag is initialized once at startup and never left unset, so the 400 below cannot actually fire for that reason in a running server — overall license validity is still enforced globally (403 on an expired license).

item.name: Get COB data for all paired devices

request.description: Returns the current COB power-mode and PCC-mode setpoint/failsafe data for every remote device paired to the HEMS's COB handler (inverter-actor controllable systems). Requires: a HEMS present. Returns an empty array when no COB device is paired or the COB handler is not initialised. The handler also checks a COB use-case-availability flag, but that flag is initialized once at startup and never left unset, so the 400 below cannot actually fire in a running server.

item.name: Send a COB PCC-mode failsafe setpoint to a device

request.description: Writes the failsafe PCC-mode setpoint (used by the device when heartbeat/ communication is lost) to the paired device's "failsafePccPowerSetpoint" configuration key. Requires: a device paired at deviceAddress exposing that key. value (Watts) is required. The EEBUS write outcome is always reported in the 200 body via success/reason; it does not change the HTTP status. The handler also checks a COB use-case-availability flag, but that flag is initialized once at startup and never left unset, so the 400 below cannot actually fire for that reason in a running server — overall license validity is still enforced globally (403 on an expired license).

item.name: Send a COB power-mode failsafe setpoint to a device

request.description: Writes the failsafe power-mode setpoint (used by the device when heartbeat/ communication is lost) to the paired device's "failsafeAcPowerSetpoint" or "failsafeDcPowerSetpoint" configuration key. Requires: a device paired at deviceAddress exposing one of those keys. value (Watts) is required. The EEBUS write outcome is always reported in the 200 body via success/reason; it does not change the HTTP status. The handler also checks a COB use-case-availability flag, but that flag is initialized once at startup and never left unset, so the 400 below cannot actually fire for that reason in a running server — overall license validity is still enforced globally (403 on an expired license).

item.name: Send a COB PCC-mode limit setpoint to a device

request.description: Writes a Coordinated Battery Optimization (COB) PCC-mode limit setpoint to the paired controllable-system device identified by deviceAddress. Requires: a remote device already paired at deviceAddress. When active is true, value (Watts) is mandatory. The EEBUS write outcome is always reported in the 200 body via success/reason; it does not change the HTTP status. The handler also checks a COB use-case-availability flag, but that flag is initialized once at startup and never left unset, so the 400 below cannot actually fire for that reason in a running server — overall license validity is still enforced globally (403 on an expired license).

item.name: Set a COB PCC-mode maximum power limit

variable.description: Which PCC maximum-power configuration key to write: AC/DC charge or discharge power maximum.

request.description: Writes one of the four PCC-mode maximum power limits to the paired device's matching device-configuration key. Requires: a device paired at deviceAddress that exposes a configuration key named after limitType. value is required, is in Watts, and is sent as-is with no range check. Unlike most COB limit routes, a failed EEBUS write is reported as HTTP 500, not 200. The handler also checks a COB use-case-availability flag, but that flag is initialized once at startup and never left unset, so the 400 below cannot actually fire for that reason in a running server — overall license validity is still enforced globally (403 on an expired license).

item.name: Send a COB power-mode limit setpoint to a device

request.description: Writes a Coordinated Battery Optimization (COB) power-mode limit setpoint to the paired controllable-system device identified by deviceAddress. Requires: a remote device already paired at deviceAddress. When active is true, value (Watts) is mandatory. The EEBUS write outcome (success or failure) is always reported in the 200 body via success/reason; it does not change the HTTP status. The handler also checks a COB use-case-availability flag, but that flag is initialized once at startup (and only re-initialized by `POST /sim` with `action: "reset"`) and is never left unset, so the 400 below cannot actually fire in a running server — overall license validity is still enforced globally (403 on an expired license).

item.name: Update the household fuse current limit

request.description:
Sets the energy meter's fuse current limit, which bounds how much current the LPC round-robin/FCFS distribution algorithms are allowed to allocate (the algorithms work against `fuseLimit * (100 - fuseSafetyMargin) / 100` per phase — see `fuseSafetyMargin` on `POST /hems/add` / `PATCH /hems`). A no-op request (value equal to the current limit) still returns 200 without emitting a config-change event.

Requires: simulation STOPPED.

item.name: Get every device (real and simulated) paired with the HEMS

request.description: Lists all remote devices currently connected to the HEMS, grouped by device with each of their SPINE entities nested underneath. Unlike `GET /hems/extDevices`, this includes both real and simulated devices. Returns an empty array `[]` (not a 404) when nothing is connected.

item.name: Get the HEMS's device-diagnosis error state

request.description: Reads back the CEM entity's local SPINE DeviceDiagnosis state (the same state written by `POST`/`DELETE` on this path). Requires the OPEV use case to be licensed/enabled.

item.name: Put the HEMS into a device-diagnosis error/failure state

request.description:
Sets the CEM entity's SPINE DeviceDiagnosis operating state to "failure" with the given `lastErrorCode`, via the OPEV feature handler (this endpoint is only usable when the OPEV use case is enabled — it is not conceptually tied to LPC/LPP but shares the OPEV DeviceDiagnosis feature instance).

Side effect on the simulation tick: while the HEMS is in this error state (or while its heartbeat is stopped, see `POST /hems/heartbeat`), the OSCEV self-consumption distribution and the OPEV round-robin/FCFS current allocation are both skipped each tick. This does **not** stop or force a transition in the LPC/LPP controllable-system state machines themselves (`myLpcCS`/`myLppCS` keep ticking and reacting to their own heartbeat/write-limit state independently of this error flag) — use `GET /hems` (`lpcState`/`lppState`) to observe those.

Requires: the OPEV use case must be licensed/enabled.

item.name: Clear the HEMS's device-diagnosis error state

request.description:
Resets the CEM entity's SPINE DeviceDiagnosis operating state back to "normalOperation" and clears the last error code (set to `"0"`). Requires the OPEV use case to be licensed/enabled.

Note: unlike the POST and GET operations on this path (which return 404 when no HEMS entity exists), this DELETE returns 400 for that same condition.

item.name: List the HEMS's connected real (external) devices

request.description: Returns the entities connected to the HEMS and, if a ControlBox is present, the ControlBox's connected entities too — filtered down to entities flagged `isExternal` (i.e. real paired devices, not simulated ones). Returns an empty array `[]` (200, not 404) when there are none.

item.name: Fetch cached data of a specific type from a connected real device

request.description:
Looks up cached remote data previously received (over SHIP/SPINE) from the real device identified by `ski`, for the requested data category. This reads from an in-memory cache populated as data arrives — it does not actively query the device. `ski` is matched as given (not normalized/lowercased like the trust endpoints).

`reqData` selects which cached dataset to return:
- `evseManufacturerData` → EVSE manufacturer/device identification.
- `currentLimits` → EV current limits.
- `currentMeasurements` → EV current measurements.
- `meterMeasurements` → external grid/submeter measurement.
- `evseFailsafeValues` → EVSE failsafe configuration.

Returns 500 if no cached data of that type exists yet for that SKI (not a client error — the device simply has not reported it, or the SKI is unknown).

item.name: Get the aggregated grid measurement and lifetime consumption/feed-in

request.description: Returns the simulated grid's current three-phase measurement plus lifetime cumulative energy totals. Note: unlike most other HEMS operations, the "no HEMS entity" case here returns 400, not 404.

item.name: Get whether the HEMS's own heartbeat is running

request.description: Reports whether the HEMS's own SPINE DeviceDiagnosis heartbeat (see `POST /hems/heartbeat`) is currently running. This is the heartbeat the HEMS *sends*; see `GET /hems/latestSentHeartbeat` for its last transmitted counter/timeout, and `GET /hems/latestReceivedHeartbeat{,/{deviceAddress}}` for heartbeats *received* from remote controllable systems.

item.name: Start or stop the HEMS's device-diagnosis heartbeat

request.description: Starts or stops the CEM entity's SPINE DeviceDiagnosis heartbeat, which is what remote controllable systems use to detect the HEMS is alive. Stopping it (or the heartbeat being lost/timed out on the remote side) is what drives a controllable system into `Failsafe` state — see `lpcState`/ `lppState` on `GET /hems`. Starting the heartbeat also clears any cached OSCEV recommendations so they are re-sent on the next distribution tick (an EV forgets its previous limits while the heartbeat is stopped).

item.name: Get OHPCF data for all connected heat pumps (real and simulated)

request.description:
Returns, for every remote device supporting OHPCF, its current OHPCF monitoring data plus the HEMS's view of whether an optional announcement is accepted and, if the heat pump has an active OHPCF process, the announced power values.

Requires: the OHPCF use case must be licensed/enabled (returns 400 otherwise).

item.name: Get the HEMS's stored display image

request.description: Returns the HEMS's stored Base64-encoded image. Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Set the HEMS's display image

request.description: Stores a Base64-encoded image for the HEMS (used by UIs for device branding). Overwrites any previously stored image; no format/size validation is performed.

item.name: Clear the HEMS's stored display image

request.description: Clears the stored image. When there was no image to begin with the call is a 400 ("no saved image") and nothing is written; when an image was present a single clean 200 is returned.

item.name: Get the latest received heartbeat from every connected remote device

request.description: Aggregates `GetLatestReceivedHeartbeat` over every remote device currently connected to the HEMS (any use case, not only LPC — contrast with `GET /hems/latestReceivedHeartbeat/{deviceAddress}`, which requires LPC and a specific address). Devices with no valid received heartbeat yet are silently omitted, so the result may have fewer entries than there are connected devices.

item.name: Get the latest heartbeat received from a specific LPC device

request.description:
Returns the counter, timeout and timestamp of the last DeviceDiagnosis heartbeat received from the LPC controllable-system device at `deviceAddress`. `deviceAddress` is looked up among the LPC remote entities specifically (this endpoint requires LPC, unlike `GET /hems/latestReceivedHeartbeat` which aggregates over all connected remote devices regardless of use case).

Requires: the LPC use case must be enabled.

item.name: Get the latest heartbeat sent by the HEMS

request.description: Returns the counter, timeout and timestamp of the last DeviceDiagnosis heartbeat the HEMS transmitted, read from the LPC feature handler if LPC is enabled, otherwise from the OPEV feature handler. This is distinct from `GET /hems/heartbeat`, which only reports whether the heartbeat loop is currently running.

item.name: Get battery manufacturer identification data (MOB use case)

request.description: Returns Monitoring of Battery identification data for every remote battery entity the HEMS's MOB handler is paired to. This route has no license/use-case gate at all (unlike MOI) and always returns 200. Fallback: when the HEMS is absent or has no remote battery paired, the response is built instead from this hub's own simulated Inverter entities (each Inverter that models a battery exposes MOB data locally) — the two sources are never mixed, remote data wins when present.

item.name: Get battery measurement data (MOB use case)

request.description: Returns Monitoring of Battery cumulative/health measurement data for every remote battery entity the HEMS's MOB handler is paired to. This route has no license/use-case gate at all and always returns 200. Fallback: when the HEMS is absent or has no remote battery paired, the response is built instead from this hub's own simulated Inverter entities.

item.name: Get battery state data (MOB use case)

request.description: Returns Monitoring of Battery state-of-charge/power data for every remote battery entity the HEMS's MOB handler is paired to. This route has no license/use-case gate at all and always returns 200. Fallback: when the HEMS is absent or has no remote battery paired, the response is built instead from this hub's own simulated Inverter entities.

item.name: Get inverter identification data (MOI use case)

request.description: Returns Monitoring of Inverter identification data for every remote inverter entity the HEMS's MOI handler is paired to. Fallback: when the HEMS is absent or has no remote inverter paired, the response is built instead from this hub's own simulated Inverter entities. The handler also checks a MOI use-case-availability flag before running, but that flag is initialized once at startup (and only re-initialized by `POST /sim` with `action: "reset"`) and is never left unset, so the 400 below cannot actually fire in a running server — overall license validity is still enforced globally (403 on an expired license). This route never returns 404 — it always answers 200, with an empty array when neither source has data.

item.name: Get inverter measurement data (MOI use case)

request.description: Returns Monitoring of Inverter power/energy measurement data for every remote inverter entity the HEMS's MOI handler is paired to. Fallback: when the HEMS is absent or has no remote inverter paired, the response is built instead from this hub's own simulated Inverter entities. Same use-case-flag caveat as `GET /hems/moi/inverterIdentification` — the 400 below is not reachable in a running server. Never returns 404; always 200, empty array when no data source is available.

item.name: Get inverter state (MOI use case)

request.description: Returns Monitoring of Inverter operating-state data for every remote inverter entity the HEMS's MOI handler is paired to. Fallback: when the HEMS is absent or has no remote inverter paired, the response is built instead from this hub's own simulated Inverter entities. Same use-case-flag caveat as `GET /hems/moi/inverterIdentification` — the 400 below is not reachable in a running server. Never returns 404; always 200, empty array when no data source is available.

item.name: get the MPS (Monitoring of PV String) data from all connected PV String entities

request.description: Returns the latest MPS data aggregated per connected PV String entity, keyed by the remote entity's device address.

item.name: Get the EVs the HEMS is connected to over OPEV

request.description: Returns the EVs the HEMS is currently connected to over the OPEV use case, sourced from the HEMS OPEV handler's remote entities (the same set the manual send validates against). An EV whose EVSE is paired to a ControlBox rather than the HEMS is not returned.

item.name: Manually send per-phase OPEV current limits to an EV

variable.description: URL-encoded SPINE entity address of the EV

request.description: Writes per-phase OPEV overload-protection current limits to the EV as a partial write. Only phases present in the body are written. The HEMS is a testing device: values are NOT range-checked and the EV's IsLimitChangeable flag is not enforced, so a tester can send arbitrary/invalid limits and observe the EV's reaction. The response reports which phases were written and which were skipped because their limit ID could not be discovered from the EV's descriptors. Requires: OPEV licensed; no simulation-state or testing-mode gate on the write itself, but the value only persists for observation instead of being immediately overwritten by the automatic round-robin/FCFS allocation if testing mode is also enabled — see `PATCH /hems/testingMode`. Discover connected EVs' addresses via `GET /hems/opev/ev/connectedData`.

item.name: Get OSCEV scenarios 5 & 6 configuration for all connected EVs

request.description: Returns the OSCEV scenario 5/6 configuration this HEMS has discovered for every remote EV it is connected to over OSCEV — the address-discovery source for `GET /hems/oscev/ev/{address}/configuration`, `.../current`, `.../power`, and `GET /hems/oscev/ev/{address}`. Requires: OSCEV licensed AND enabled on this HEMS instance.

item.name: Get discovered OSCEV state for an EV

variable.description: URL-encoded SPINE entity address of the EV

request.description: Returns the HEMS's tracked OSCEV state for one EV: the last recommendation this HEMS sent it (current or power) and the scenario 5/6 configuration last discovered from it. `address` is a SPINE entity address — discover connected EVs' addresses via `GET /hems/oscev/ev/configurationData` or `GET /hems/opev/ev/connectedData`. Requires: OSCEV licensed AND enabled on this HEMS instance.

item.name: Get OSCEV scenarios 5 & 6 configuration for an EV

variable.description: URL-encoded SPINE entity address of the EV

request.description: Returns the OSCEV scenario 5 (PV charge mode / surplus threshold) and scenario 6 (start/stop delay) configuration this HEMS most recently discovered from the EV at address. Requires: OSCEV licensed AND enabled on this HEMS instance.

item.name: Write OSCEV scenarios 5 & 6 configuration to an EV

variable.description: URL-encoded SPINE entity address of the EV

request.description: Writes any subset of OSCEV scenario 5/6 configuration fields to the EV at address — only the fields present (non-null) in the body are written. Requires: OSCEV licensed AND enabled on this HEMS instance. `surplusThresholdInWatts`, `startDelayInSeconds` and `stopDelayInSeconds` are each rejected with 400 if negative; there is no upper bound check.

item.name: Send a per-phase OSCEV current recommendation to an EV

variable.description: URL-encoded SPINE entity address of the EV

request.description: Sends a per-phase OSCEV current recommendation. Only phases present in the body are written (partial write), and each phase's IsLimitActive is honored independently (send isLimitActive=false to deactivate a phase). The HEMS is a testing device: values are NOT range-checked, so negative / out-of-range values are allowed. Requires: OSCEV licensed AND enabled on this HEMS instance. Discover connected EVs' addresses via `GET /hems/oscev/ev/configurationData`.

item.name: Send OSCEV power recommendation to an EV

variable.description: URL-encoded SPINE entity address of the EV

request.description: Sends an OSCEV power recommendation, or deactivates the previously sent one (active=false — the deviceAddress must still resolve, but no value is required and none is sent). The HEMS is a testing device: the value is NOT range-checked and the EV's scenario-4 support is NOT required, so a tester can send a power recommendation to an EV that does not advertise scenario 4 (or an out-of-range value) and observe how it responds. Sending a power recommendation clears any previously tracked current recommendation for the EV, and vice versa (OSCEV-044 — only one of the two is active at a time). Requires: OSCEV licensed AND enabled on this HEMS instance.

item.name: Get HEMS OSCEV state

request.description: Reports the HEMS's own OSCEV (Optimization of Self-Consumption During EV Charging) operating state — the SPINE DeviceDiagnosis operating state the HEMS itself publishes, which paired EVs can observe — and whether its OSCEV heartbeat is currently running. Requires: OSCEV licensed AND enabled on this HEMS instance (the `oscevEnabled` flag passed to `POST /hems/add` / `PATCH /hems`) — both are checked on every call, unlike the dead use-case-availability flags described elsewhere in this group; either failing returns 403.

item.name: Update HEMS OSCEV operating state

request.description: Sets the HEMS's own OSCEV operating state and republishes it on the bus; connected EVs observing the HEMS's DeviceDiagnosis operating state pick up the change. Setting "failure" is how a tester simulates the HEMS losing its ability to optimize self-consumption. Requires: OSCEV licensed AND enabled on this HEMS instance, checked on every call (403 if either is false).

item.name: Get the HEMS's SHIP QR-code pairing text

request.description: Returns the SHIP QR-code pairing string for the HEMS's own service (SKI, host and port encoded per the SHIP QR-code format), for use by a real device's manual-pairing / QR-scan flow. Complements `POST /hems/trust`, which is the reverse direction (HEMS trusting a remote SKI).

item.name: Get testing mode

request.description: Reports whether testing mode is active. While active, the automatic OPEV round-robin/first-come-first-served allocation and the automatic OSCEV self-consumption distribution tick are both suspended (see the HEMS `Simulate` loop), so limit/recommendation writes sent manually — `PATCH /hems/opev/ev/{address}/current`, `PATCH /hems/oscev/ev/{address}/current`, `PATCH /hems/oscev/ev/{address}/power` — persist for observation instead of being overwritten on the next tick. Requires: none — no license or simulation-state gate; available whenever a HEMS entity exists.

item.name: Enable or disable testing mode

request.description: Toggles testing mode. Requires: none — no license or simulation-state gate; available whenever a HEMS entity exists. See `GET /hems/testingMode` for what testing mode suspends.

item.name: Trust a remote device's SKI on the HEMS

request.description:
Registers `remoteSki` as a trusted SHIP peer on the HEMS's service, so the real or simulated device holding that SKI can pair with it. `remoteSki` is normalized before use — surrounding/embedded whitespace is stripped and the value is lowercased; no length or hex-charset check is performed, so a malformed SKI is only rejected if it becomes empty after normalization.

This is one half of a mutual-trust pairing: the device side must trust the HEMS's own SKI too (see the corresponding trust endpoint for the target entity type, e.g. `POST /evse/{id}/trust`, or `POST /trust` for the two-sided form). Use `GET /mdns` to discover a real device's SKI before trusting it, or `GET /hems/qr-code` to get the HEMS's SKI/pairing data.

Requires: the simulation must not be in the brief transitional "stopping" window after `POST /sim` `action: stop` (`Engine.isAllowedToPairDevices`) — a simulation that has never been started, or is fully stopped, is accepted. 400 "Simulation not running" otherwise (the error message is misleading given the actual condition).

item.name: Untrust (disconnect) a remote device's SKI on the HEMS

request.description:
Disconnects any active SHIP connection to `remoteSki` and removes it from the HEMS's trusted-peer list. `remoteSki` is normalized the same way as `POST /hems/trust` (whitespace stripped, lowercased).

Unlike `POST /hems/trust`, this endpoint does not require the simulation to be running — it can be called at any time as long as the HEMS entity exists.

item.name: Get the registered real HEMS SKI

request.description: Always returns 200. Returns `{remoteSKI, imgBase64}` if an external HEMS was registered via `POST /hems/addExt`, or an empty array `[]` (not a 404) if none has been registered yet.

item.name: Update the registered real HEMS SKI and/or image

request.description: Replaces the registered external HEMS's SKI and/or image. Unlike `GET /hemsExt`'s response and `POST /hems/addExt`'s request (which both use `remoteSKI`, all caps), this request body's SKI field is `remoteSki` (lower-case "ki") — a casing inconsistency in the underlying types. The SKI is **not** normalized/lowercased here (unlike `POST /hems/addExt` and `POST /hems/trust`). Changing the SKI while the simulation is running is rejected with 400; the image can be changed at any time. Any unrecognized field (e.g. `deviceName`) is silently ignored.

item.name: Remove the registered real HEMS SKI

request.description: Requires: simulation STOPPED. Blocked with 409 while a test run is active (see `POST /testrun`), unless the request carries a valid test-run token.

item.description: The singleton Home Energy Management System (CEM) — pairing, limits (LPC/LPP), monitoring, and use-case control.

item.name: Heat Pump
Get OHPCF monitor data for every heat pump that announced a process

request.description: Iterates every heat pump entity and includes only those that have announced an optional power-consumption process — see `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/announceOptional` (`HeatPump.HasAnnouncedOptionalProcess`); a heat pump that has never announced is omitted entirely, not returned with empty data. This is a heat-pump-only view; the equivalent all-devices endpoint `GET /hems/OhpcfMonitorData` covers the same use case from the CEM side. Requires: the OHPCF use case must be enabled by the license — 400 otherwise.

item.name: Add a new heat pump to the simulation

request.description:
Creates a simulated heat pump entity with its own EEBUS service (SHIP/SPINE not started until it is trusted — see `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/trust`).

Requires: simulation STOPPED (400 otherwise). `deviceName` must be unique across every existing heat pump, and the `(vendor.code, serialNumber, deviceModel)` triple must also be unique (400 "Device name already exists" / "Device address already exists"). Body validation (see `HeatPumpInfo` for the exact bounds): `deviceName`, `brandName`, `deviceCode`, `serialNumber`, `vendor.code` and `vendor.name` must be non-empty; `failsafeValue` >= 0; `failsafeDuration` and `failsafeDurationMax` in [2, 24] hours; `nominalPower` and `nominalCurrent` are both required objects (despite being optional in the schema) with `min`/`max` >= 0, `min < max` within each, and `nominalCurrent.min < nominalPower.max` — a genuine cross-field constraint, not a units mismatch. On validation failure, the 400 body's `err` is not a string but an object whose keys are the names of the fields that failed (each mapped to the literal value `false`) — e.g. `{"err": {"failsafeDuration": false}}`.

Two fields in the request body are silently overridden and not honored as sent: `brandName` is always forced to `"Coretech-Innovations"`, and `lpcEnabled`/`mpcEnabled` are overwritten from the server's license-derived use-case availability when that value is set (see the per-use-case nil checks noted throughout this specification — in practice only an expired license's 403 meaningfully blocks use-case availability, these overrides rarely change behavior for a valid license). `trustConnections` (if supplied) is validated against the device-role rules — a heat pump is a controllable device, so every peer must resolve to a controller (HEMS or ControlBox) — and recorded the same way as `POST /trust`.

item.name: Get list of all heat pumps

request.description: Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Get heat pump details by ID

request.description: Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Update heat pump configuration

request.description: Applies the same validation as `POST /heatpump/add` (see there for the exact bounds and the error-object shape) except the uniqueness check on deviceName/device-address ignores this heat pump's own current record. `brandName` is preserved from the existing configuration regardless of what the request sends (not overridden to a fixed value like on create). If the merged configuration is byte-for-byte identical to the current one, the handler returns 200 immediately without touching the entity or logging a change. No check on simulation state — unlike add/delete, this endpoint may be called while the simulation is running.

item.name: Delete a heat pump

header.description: Internal token used by test automation to bypass the active-test-run block.

request.description: Requires: simulation STOPPED (400 otherwise). Same test-run-active guard as every other destructive endpoint: blocked with 409 while a compliance test run is active, unless the request carries a valid `X-EEBUS-Internal-Test-Token`.

item.name: Get the LPC active power consumption limit applied to the heat pump

request.description:
Returns the LPC Active Power Consumption Limit (APCL) currently reported by the heat pump (`HeatPump.GetActivePowerLimit`) — an object (`active`, `value`, `durationSeconds`, ...), not a bare number. Requires: the heat pump must have a controllable system (LPC enabled) — 400 ("no LPC supported") otherwise.

Note the path here is `activePowerLimit`, with no `lpc` prefix — the equivalent EVSE and Inverter endpoints are named `/evse/{evseId}/lpcActivePowerLimit` and `/inverter/{inverterId}/lpc/lpcActivePowerLimit`. This is purely a naming difference; the underlying data (`lpcAPCL`) is identical.

item.name: Announce an optional OHPCF power-consumption process (OHPCF Scenario 1, Phase A)

request.description:
Publishes a `SmartEnergyManagementPsData` announcement over SPINE (`AnnounceOptionalProcess` → `applyAnnouncementLocked`) — this is what makes the heat pump visible in `GET /hems/OhpcfMonitorData` and `GET /heatpump/OhpcfMonitorData` (both filter to heat pumps that have announced) and populates the `Alternatives` array a connected HEMS reads. The new process always starts in state `inactive`, and any previous schedule/start time is cleared as a side effect.

Validation (`validateAnnouncementParams`, EEBUS rule references in brackets): rejected with 400 if another process is already scheduled/running/paused [OHPCF-013] — complete or force-abort it first (see `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/setState` / `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/forceOhpcfState`); at least one of `isPausable`/`isStoppable` must be true; `activeDurationMinSeconds` and `pauseDurationMinSeconds` are both required (non-negative numbers); at least one of `power`/`powerMax` is required; the heat pump must have `nominalPower` configured (see `HeatPumpInfo`); any supplied `power`/`powerMax` must be > 0 and within `[nominalPower.min, nominalPower.max]`, and `power` (if both are set) must not exceed `powerMax`.

item.name: Get electrical measurements (MPC)

request.description: Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Force the HeatPump OHPCF power-sequence state (testing aid)

request.description:
Inject the heat pump's OHPCF power-sequence state directly, bypassing the transition table `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/setState` enforces. Internally this reuses the normal announcement path (the same code `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/announceOptional` calls) to set up the announced power, then sets the state; the next simulate tick treats it as a genuine entry and the OHPCF state machine resumes (auto-advance timers + CEM start-time handling).

Requires: the heat pump must already be in testing mode (`PATCH /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/mode` with `testingMode: true`) — 400 otherwise. Per target `state`: `running`/`scheduled`/`paused` need a power value (`powerMaxInWatts` in the request, or a prior announcement already in place); `scheduled` additionally needs `startDelayInSeconds`; `completed`/`invalid` need a prior announcement to already exist; `inactive` needs nothing. When `powerMaxInWatts` is supplied, the resulting announcement must still satisfy the pausable/stoppable requirement (at least one of `isPausable`/`isStoppable` must resolve to true, falling back to the heat pump's config then to defaults — see `OhpcfForceStateRequest`).

item.name: Force the HeatPump controllable-system state (testing aid)

request.description:
Inject the heat pump's LPC controllable system into a chosen state once, so a tester can start a scenario with the device already in that state. The real state machine resumes on the next tick — incoming limit writes are processed and transitions out of the forced state follow the normal FSM. See CSState for what each of the five states means.

Requires: the heat pump must have a controllable system (LPC enabled), AND the heat pump must already be in testing mode (`PATCH /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/mode` with `testingMode: true`) — both are checked, and either missing returns 400. This is a one-shot injection: it is applied on the next simulate tick and is not re-applied afterwards.

request.description: Overwrites the heat pump's `imgBase64` unconditionally (no validation of the string content). Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Delete heat pump image

request.description: Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route). Both the not-found and the no-image case return their response and change nothing.

item.name: Get the last LPC heartbeat the heat pump received from the CEM

request.description: Requires: the heat pump must have a controllable system (LPC enabled) — 400 ("LPC use case support is disabled") otherwise.

item.name: Get the last LPC heartbeat the heat pump sent

request.description: Requires: the heat pump must have a controllable system (LPC enabled) — 400 ("LPC use case support is disabled") otherwise.

item.name: Get the heat pump's LPC controllable-system state

request.description: Returns the heat pump's LPC controllable-system FSM state (`HeatPump.GetCurrentState`). `currentState` is the empty string if the heat pump has no controllable system (LPC disabled) — this is not an error. See CSState for the meaning of each value. Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Get the heat pump's LPC failsafe active power consumption limit

request.description: Returns the failsafe power limit/duration configured on this heat pump (derived from `failsafeValue`/`failsafeDuration` on `HeatPumpInfo`, applied by the controllable system when the CEM's heartbeat is lost — see CSState's `Failsafe` value). Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Get LPC power constraints

request.description: Requires: the heat pump must have a controllable system (LPC enabled) — 400 ("LPC use case support is disabled") otherwise.

item.name: Get the heat pump simulation/testing mode and pinned power

request.description: `mode` is "simulation" (default, reported values derived from the simulation) or "testing" (reported values pinned to whatever was last set via `PATCH /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/values`). `live` always reports the currently effective readings, whichever mode is active. `ohpcfState` mirrors the OHPCF power-sequence state (empty only when OHPCF is not supported at all) — see `OhpcfMonitorData` for the reachable values.

item.name: Toggle the heat pump simulation/testing mode

request.description: Switches the heat pump between simulation and testing mode only. The pinned override values are set separately via PATCH /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/values. Enabling testing mode snapshots the current power so the device reports it verbatim until specific values are pinned; disabling clears all pins.

item.name: Get one heat pump's OHPCF monitor data

request.description: Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route). Unlike `GET /heatpump/OhpcfMonitorData`, this always returns data — even a heat pump that has never announced a process reports `state: "inactive"` rather than being omitted or erroring, because `GetOhpcfMonitorData` never returns nil. The 404 "OHPCF not enabled" case documented informally elsewhere for this handler is unreachable in the current implementation for that reason — the only 404 this endpoint actually produces is an unknown `heatPumpId`.

item.name: Get SHIP QR-pairing data for the heat pump

request.description: Returns the SHIP QR-code pairing text for the heat pump's own EEBUS service. Requires: the heat pump's service must already be running (started via `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/trust` or otherwise) — 400 ("service not initialized") otherwise. A malformed `heatPumpId`, and a `heatPumpId` resolving to a non-heat-pump entity, both return 400; 404 is reserved for a `heatPumpId` that resolves to no entity at all.

item.name: Get remote devices connected to this heat pump

request.description: Returns the SPINE devices currently connected/paired to this heat pump's own EEBUS service, with each device's SKI, address, supported use cases and exposed feature types. Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Transition the heat pump's OHPCF power-sequence state

request.description:
Applies a validated OHPCF state transition via the same local path a connected HEMS's SPINE write would use (`myOhpcfHandler.SetPowerSequenceState`), without going through SPINE — this is a REST-side equivalent of the write, not a proxy for a remote write. The allowed transitions (`ohpcfAllowedTransitions`) are:

  - `scheduled` → `invalid` (only)
  - `running` → `completed` or `invalid`
  - `paused` → `invalid` (only)
  - `inactive` and `completed`/`invalid` have **no** outgoing transitions at
    all — there is deliberately no entry for `inactive` as a start state, so
    a freshly-announced (or never-announced) process cannot be moved to
    `scheduled`/`running` through this endpoint. Use
    `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/forceOhpcfState` (testing mode only) to
    force a state directly instead.

Any transition not in this table — including everything out of `inactive` — is rejected with 400. This table is deliberately narrower than what a remote CEM's SPINE write is allowed to request (the write-approval callback additionally permits `running`→`paused` and `paused`→`running`, gated on `isPausable`/`isStoppable` and minimum active/pause durations); those richer transitions are not reachable through this REST endpoint.

item.name: Trust a remote device from the heat pump side (imperative SKI pairing)

request.description:
Registers `remoteSki` as trusted for pairing on this heat pump's own SHIP service, starting that service first if it has not run yet. This is the imperative, one-shot counterpart to the declarative `POST /trust` / `trustConnections` mechanism (see `GET /trust`): it acts on a single, already-identified entity immediately, rather than recording a desired relationship the engine re-applies on every `POST /sim` start. This is one half of mutual trust — the peer (e.g. the HEMS/CEM) must also trust this heat pump's SKI (`ski` in the response, or `GetHeatPump`'s `ski` field) on its own side for pairing to actually complete.

Requires: the simulation must not be in the brief transitional "stopping" window after `POST /sim` `action: stop` is called (`Engine.isAllowedToPairDevices` — despite its name this is **not** "simulation must be running": it also returns true while the simulation has never been started, or is fully stopped; only the few seconds while a Stop() teardown is in flight return false). 400 "Simulation not running" otherwise (the error message is misleading given the actual condition).

If starting the heat pump's EEBUS service fails (`hpEntity.Run()` returns an error, attempted only when the local SKI is not yet set), the call is a 500 and no SKI is registered.

item.name: Set the heat pump forced measurement values (testing mode only)

request.description: Pins the heat pump's reported power/current/voltage/frequency verbatim. Requires testing mode (400 otherwise). Every field optional.

List every uncontrollable device

request.description: Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Add a fixed-load uncontrollable device (e.g. dishwasher, dryer)

request.description:
Creates a simple simulated load with no EEBUS presence of its own: no SPINE service, no use cases, nothing to pair or trust. It exists purely to draw a configured per-phase current whenever `powerStateOn` is true, so that LPC/OPEV/etc. scenarios can be tested against a household with background load. `deviceName` defaults to `"my device"` if omitted or empty. A negative current on any phase is rejected; an out-of-range `powerFactor` (<= 0 or > 1) is silently coerced to 1.0 rather than rejected.

Requires: simulation STOPPED (400 otherwise).

item.name: Update an uncontrollable device's configuration

request.description:
Applies only the top-level keys present in the request body (`deviceName`, `powerStateOn`, `current`, `powerFactor`); a `current` object may set any subset of `a`/`b`/`c`, leaving the others unchanged. The 200 response is written immediately after binding the body — before the per-key changes are actually applied to the entity — so `new` always reflects the fully-merged request body, whether or not it turned out to be a no-op.

Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route). No check on simulation state — unlike POST/DELETE on this tag, this endpoint may be called while the simulation is running.

item.name: Delete an uncontrollable device

header.description: Internal token used by test automation to bypass the active-test-run block.

request.description: Requires: simulation STOPPED (400 otherwise — note the handler's error message says "can not add uncontrollable device while simulation is running", a copy/paste artifact from the POST handler; the check itself is genuinely for delete). Same test-run-active guard as every other destructive endpoint: blocked with 409 while a compliance test run is active, unless the request carries a valid `X-EEBUS-Internal-Test-Token`.

item.name: Get an uncontrollable device's stored image

request.description: Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Set an uncontrollable device's image

request.description: Overwrites `imgBase64` unconditionally (no validation of the string content). Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Clear an uncontrollable device's stored image

request.description: Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route). When there is no saved image the call is a 404 and nothing is written; otherwise the image is cleared and the call is a 200.
