item.name: Energy Meter
Get the simulated grid-connection meter's live per-phase readings

request.description:
Returns the singleton `EnergyMeter`'s current grid measurement — the point the simulation treats as the physical grid connection (household fuse), fed by summing every simulated/connected device's power draw/feed-in each engine tick (`internal.GridBUS`). This is a different meter from the `Internal Meter` tag's Modbus meter (`GET /internalmeter/readings`): this one reflects the simulation's own bookkeeping, the Modbus meter is a protocol-level replica of it exposed to an external HEMS. `fuseLimit` (used to abort the simulation via `POST /sim` when any phase's uncontrollable-device current exceeds it — see `internal.Engine.validateTotalCurrents`) is internal engine state and is not part of this response.

Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.description: Aggregated energy meter view of the simulated site.

item.name: Internal Meter
Get InternalMeter status (config + running state + mode)

request.description: Returns the singleton Modbus-meter's pure configuration (`info`) plus derived state: `running` (is the Modbus TCP server currently accepting connections) and `mode` (`live` — readings are derived from the simulation's EnergyMeter each tick, or `forced` — readings are pinned via `PUT /internalmeter/readings`). This is a distinct device from the `Energy Meter` tag's `GET /energymeter`: this one is a Modbus TCP server (SDM630/SMA Home Manager register layout) an external HEMS can poll as if it were a real meter; `GET /energymeter` is the simulation's own internal grid measurement, consumed only over this REST API.

item.name: Update InternalMeter configuration

request.description:
Updates meter configuration. Transport-level fields (modbusHost, modbusPort, unitId)
are rejected while a simulation is running. If transport fields change and the server
is running it is restarted automatically on the new address. Omitted fields in the
request body are pre-filled from the current configuration before validation, so a
partial body (e.g. just `serialNumber`) does not fail validation on the fields it
left out — this is a PATCH in effect even though the request re-sends the full
`InternalMeterInfo` shape.

item.name: Get current meter readings snapshot (what a Modbus client would read)

request.description: Returns the same snapshot the Modbus TCP server would serve to a connected client over the wire, decoded to JSON — useful for inspecting/asserting on readings without a Modbus client. Reflects whichever mode is currently active (`live` or `forced`, see `GET /internalmeter`).

item.name: Force meter readings (switches meter to forced mode)

request.description:
Pins all meter values to the supplied body. The meter enters "forced" mode;
energy counters continue advancing each engine tick using the supplied power value.
Pass only the fields you want to pin — omitted numeric fields default to 0.
Every energy accumulator (total and per-phase import/export) is re-seeded from
the supplied snapshot on this call, so switching modes never produces a
discontinuity in the energy counters.

item.name: Clear forced readings and return to live mode

request.description:
Clears any forced override. Voltage/frequency/PF immediately return to
nominal-idle values; power and current return to 0 until the next engine
tick. Accumulated energy is preserved — counters never go backwards.

item.name: Start the InternalMeter Modbus TCP server

request.description: Starts listening on `modbusHost:modbusPort` (unit `unitId`). No-op (still 200) if already running. Requires the `modbusMeter` license feature — 403 even before the generic license check would otherwise apply, because this route also has an explicit feature-license guard in the handler (`HubLicense.IsModbusMeterSupported()`), independent of the entity/use-case gating every other route in this specification relies on.

item.name: Stop the InternalMeter Modbus TCP server

request.description: Stops the Modbus TCP listener. No-op (still 200) if already stopped.

item.description: The Hub's internal metering service and its readings.

item.name: Real Devices
Register a real (non-simulated) device under test by SKI and type

request.description:
Registers a physical/external device so the Hub can track it and (optionally) pre-wire trust connections to simulated peers before the simulation starts. This does not itself pair or start any SHIP connection — it only records the device's SKI/type/name in the `RealDevicesHandler` registry; actual pairing happens the same way as for any other peer, via the trust mechanisms below.

Requires: simulation STOPPED (400 otherwise). `remoteSki` must be a 40-character SKI (400 otherwise) and must not already be registered (400, "the Entered SKI is already Registered"). `deviceType` must be one of the 14 accepted values (400 "invalid device type" otherwise — see the `realDevice` schema's `deviceType` enum). At most one real device of type `EnergyManagementSystem` may ever be registered, and only if no simulated HEMS currently exists (400 otherwise) — a real device and a simulated HEMS are mutually exclusive, and only one real HEMS is supported. If `trustConnections` is supplied, every entry must reference a simulated peer by `id` (a real device cannot be wired to another real device — the Hub does not control either side's hardware to establish trust) and must pass the same device-role validation as `POST /trust` (see `TrustPeerRef`); on success each connection is recorded exactly as if `POST /trust` had been called with `{ski: remoteSki}` as one endpoint — see `GET /trust` for how the two mechanisms relate.

item.name: Get one registered real device by type and id

variable.description: One of the 14 SPINE device types accepted by `RealDevicesHandler.ValidateDeviceType` (internal/realDevices.go). Any other value is rejected with 400 ("invalid device type").

request.description: `deviceId` is scoped per `deviceType` — ids are assigned independently within each type's own registry (see `POST /realDevice`), so `deviceId=0` can identify a different device under a different `deviceType`.

item.name: Replace the stored image for a real device

variable.description: One of the 14 SPINE device types accepted by `RealDevicesHandler.ValidateDeviceType` (internal/realDevices.go). Any other value is rejected with 400 ("invalid device type").

request.description: Overwrites the device's `imgBase64` field. Unlike the simulated-device image endpoints (e.g. `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/image`), there is no separate GET/DELETE for a real device's image and no validation on the supplied string — an empty value clears it. This is the only mutable field on a real device; SKI/name/type are fixed at `POST /realDevice` time.

item.name: Unregister a real device

header.description: Internal token used by test automation to bypass the active-test-run block.

variable.description: One of the 14 SPINE device types accepted by `RealDevicesHandler.ValidateDeviceType` (internal/realDevices.go). Any other value is rejected with 400 ("invalid device type").

request.description:
Removes the device from the registry and drops every trust edge that references its SKI (`TrustManager.RemoveEdgesFor`) — including edges the Hub established automatically after out-of-band pairing, not just ones added via `trustConnections`/`POST /trust`.

Requires: simulation STOPPED (400 otherwise). Same test-run-active guard as every other destructive endpoint: blocked with 409 while a compliance test run is active, unless the request carries a valid `X-EEBUS-Internal-Test-Token`.

item.name: List every registered real device, across all device types

request.description:
Returns all real devices registered via `POST /realDevice`, regardless of `deviceType`, sorted by `remoteSki`. Returns an empty array (not an error) both when the registry has not been initialised yet and when it has no entries.

Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.description: Registration and management of real (non-simulated) EEBUS devices.

item.name: Testing
List EEBUS services discovered on the network via mDNS

request.description: Returns the hub's live mDNS scan results, used to help a user pick a DUT's SKI/host without typing it by hand before POST /testing/dut/environment. Simulated hub entities are suppressed from the list by default (see the `--mdnsnosuppres` flag); this is a read-only convenience lookup, not a requirement of the run lifecycle.

item.name: Get the configured DUT connection settings

request.description: Step 1 of the compliance run lifecycle: DUT identity (`ski`, `shipId`) and connection (`rpcUrl`) must be set — via POST to this same path — before test-case selection (POST /testing/selection) or execution (POST /testing/execute) can succeed. Returns zero-value fields until configured.

item.name: Configure the DUT connection settings

request.description: Sets the DUT SKI, SHIP pairing ID, and JSON-RPC address the compliance pipeline will drive during a run. `ski` is normalized (whitespace stripped, lowercased) and must resolve to 40 hex characters or the request is rejected. `rpcUrl` must be `host:port`; live reachability is not checked here — poll GET /testing/rpc-server/status separately, or rely on the pre-run probe performed by POST /testing/execute. Requires: the compliance-tests license feature, and no test run currently active (400 if one is running or cancelling; see GET /testing/run/status). Side effect: persists to `testingConfiguration.json` and emits an SSE `testingUpdate` event.

item.name: Get the configured DUT test parameters

request.description: Returns the DUT's electrical/timing parameters (nominal power, failsafe limits, MPC capabilities, …) used to parameterize compliance test cases. Returns `null` until configured via POST to this same path. Only the subset of fields required by the current selection (GET /testing/required-config) needs to be set before a run; unrelated fields may be omitted.

item.name: Configure the DUT test parameters

request.description: Step 2 of the compliance run lifecycle (after POST /testing/dut/environment): sets the DUT power/timing/MPC-capability values the selected test cases need. Only fields required by the current suite/test-case selection are validated — see GET /testing/required-config for the field list, which changes as the selection (POST /testing/selection) changes. Validated ranges include `dutFailsafeDurationMaxSeconds` (7200–86400 s), non-negative limit/duration fields, and min ≤ max pairing between the nominal-power and active-power-limit fields. Requires: the compliance-tests license feature, and no test run currently active (400 if one is running or cancelling). Side effect: persists to `testingConfiguration.json` and emits an SSE `testingUpdate` event.

item.name: Start the compliance run for the current selection

request.description: Step 4 (final) of the compliance run lifecycle. Validates that every `requiredConfigFields` entry for the current selection (GET /testing/required-config) has been explicitly set via POST /testing/dut/test-config — no silent defaults are applied — then clears the log buffer and starts the run asynchronously: the hub first re-probes the DUT RPC server (see GET /testing/rpc-server/status) and fails the run immediately if it is unreachable, then drives the compliance pipeline in the background. Poll GET /testing/run/status for progress and per-test-case results, GET /testing/logs or /testing/logs/stream for live output, and GET /testing/report once the run finishes. Side effect: while a run is active, every simulation-mutating endpoint under `/sim` and every device-add/configure endpoint returns 409 unless the caller presents a matching `X-EEBUS-Internal-Test-Token` header (checked against the `EEBUS_HUB_INTERNAL_TEST_TOKEN` environment variable) — this lets the compliance pipeline itself keep driving the simulation while ordinary API clients are locked out for the duration of the run. Requires: the compliance-tests license feature, a configured DUT (POST /testing/dut/environment), a non-empty selection (POST /testing/selection), the HEMS entity to exist, and no run already in progress.

item.name: Request cancellation of the active run

request.description: Signals the running compliance pipeline to stop scheduling further test cases. The run does not stop instantly: the in-progress test case is allowed to finish, `status` moves to `cancelling` immediately (visible via GET /testing/run/status) and settles to `failed` once the pipeline actually unwinds. Requires: a run currently in the `running` state — 409 if idle, already `cancelling`, `completed`, or `failed`.

item.name: Get buffered test execution logs, or upgrade to a log WebSocket

query.description: Number of latest entries to return. Returns all if omitted or invalid.

request.description:
NOTE: this endpoint streams and does not complete on its own. Send it interactively and cancel when done; do not include it in a Collection Runner.

Dual-mode endpoint. A plain GET returns the last `limit` buffered log entries (ring buffer of 500) as a JSON array — a one-shot snapshot, no data is added. If the request carries WebSocket upgrade headers (`Connection: Upgrade`, `Upgrade: websocket`), the handler instead upgrades the connection: it first replays the full current buffer, then pushes each new entry as JSON as the active run produces it, and sends periodic pings to keep the socket alive across proxies. Logs are cleared at the start of every new run (POST /testing/execute), and any WebSocket subscriptions open from a previous run are closed at that point so they cannot bleed into the new run's log stream. For a plain-HTTP alternative to the WebSocket, see GET /testing/logs/stream (Server-Sent Events).

item.name: Clear buffered test execution logs

request.description:
Empties the in-memory test execution log buffer so a later WebSocket (or REST) read only returns entries produced after this call.

Requires: nothing beyond a valid license; the buffer exists whether or not a test run is active, and clearing it while one is running simply drops the entries produced so far.

item.name: Download the full execution log of the current or last test run

request.description: Serves the complete execution log file of the current or most recent test run as a `text/plain` attachment. Unlike GET /testing/logs, whose in-memory buffer only keeps the latest 500 entries, this file holds every entry of the run, one per line as `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] [LEVEL] message`, with the timestamp in the hub's local time. Available while a run is still active (the file then contains the entries produced so far). DELETE /testing/logs does not affect it. Requires: at least one run started since the hub was launched (POST /testing/execute) — 404 otherwise, or if the log file is missing on disk.

item.name: Stream test execution logs over Server-Sent Events

request.description:
NOTE: this endpoint streams and does not complete on its own. Send it interactively and cancel when done; do not include it in a Collection Runner.

SSE alternative to the WebSocket upgrade offered by GET /testing/logs — plain `text/event-stream`, no upgrade handshake required, so it works through infrastructure that blocks WebSockets. Does not replay buffered history: only log entries produced after the connection opens are sent, each as an `event: testingLog` frame whose `data` is a JSON `testingExecutionLog` object. Closed automatically when a new run starts (see GET /testing/logs for the shared close-on-new-run behavior).

item.name: Download the HTML report for the last finished run

request.description: Serves the Ginkgo-generated `report.html` for the most recently finished run (inline, `Content-Disposition: inline`). Requires: no test run currently active — 409 while `status` is `running` or `cancelling` (see GET /testing/run/status); 404 if no run has ever completed, or if the report file for the last run is missing on disk.

item.name: Get the DUT test-config fields the current selection needs

request.description: Returns the union, over every suite and individual test case in the current selection (POST /testing/selection), of the DUT test-configuration field names each one declares as required (see `requiredConfigFields` on each entry from GET /testing/testcases). Field names use the hub's external naming — notably `dutIsHEMS` rather than the compliance pipeline's internal `dutIsCEM`. POST /testing/dut/test-config and POST /testing/execute both re-derive this same set server-side to decide what must be present, so this endpoint is a read-only convenience for building the DUT test-config form.

item.name: Probe the DUT RPC server for reachability

request.description: Performs a live TCP dial (`net.DialTimeout`, 2 s timeout) to the `rpcUrl` configured via POST /testing/dut/environment on every call and reports whether a listener accepted the connection. Safe to poll — the same probe backs a 2 s background monitor that fires the `rpcServerStatusUpdate` SSE event (see GET /events) whenever reachability flips, so the UI does not have to poll this endpoint continuously. Returns `reachable: false` with `host`/`port` omitted (no dial attempted) when no `rpcUrl` is configured for the DUT. This same reachability check runs once, synchronously, at the start of POST /testing/execute — a run fails immediately if it does not pass.

item.name: Poll the active test run's progress and per-test-case results

request.description: Poll this while a run is in progress (started by POST /testing/execute) to drive a progress bar and a per-test-case results table. `status` transitions idle → running → (completed|failed), or running → cancelling → failed when POST /testing/execute/cancel is called. `progress` is the percentage of selected test cases that have finished (passed, failed, or skipped) — recomputed after every test-case completion event, not a wall-clock estimate. `testCases` mirrors the compliance pipeline's per-case status list, seeded from the current selection when the run starts. Cross-ref: GET /testing/logs/stream for live log lines during the run, GET /testing/report for the HTML report once the run finishes.

item.name: Get the selected suites and test cases

request.description: Returns the current selection set by POST to this same path. `testCaseIds` never duplicates a test case already covered by an entry in `suites` — selecting a suite absorbs any individually selected test case that belongs to it (see POST, below).

item.name: Select suites and/or individual test cases to run

request.description: Step 3 of the compliance run lifecycle: chooses which suites (`suites`, e.g. `lpc-cs`) and/or individual test cases (`testCaseIds`, e.g. `LPC_T001`) POST /testing/execute will run. Replaces the whole selection (not additive) and normalizes it — entries are de-duplicated and sorted, and any `testCaseIds` entry already covered by a selected suite is dropped since the suite selection already implies it. Selecting new suites/test cases changes the union of `requiredConfigFields` returned by GET /testing/required-config, which in turn determines which fields POST /testing/dut/test-config must supply. Requires: the compliance-tests license feature, every requested suite/test case allowed by it, and no test run currently active. Side effect: emits an SSE `testingUpdate` event.

item.name: Clear the entire selection

request.description: Empties both `suites` and `testCaseIds`. Requires: no test run currently active. Side effect: emits an SSE `testingUpdate` event only when the selection actually changed.

item.name: Deselect one suite

request.description: Removes a single suite from the current selection (see POST /testing/selection) without touching individually selected test cases from other suites. Requires: no test run currently active. 404 if `suite` is not currently selected. Side effect: emits an SSE `testingUpdate` event.

item.name: Deselect one individual test case

request.description: Removes a single test case from the current selection (see POST /testing/selection). If `testCaseId` is currently selected only indirectly — via a suite selection that covers it — that suite is replaced with the rest of its test cases so the target case alone drops out. Requires: no test run currently active. 404 if `testCaseId` is not currently selected (directly or via a suite). Side effect: emits an SSE `testingUpdate` event.

item.name: Get the testing dashboard overview

request.description: Returns the DUT identity/config, the current suite/test-case selection, and the run lifecycle state in one call — the snapshot used to render the Testing page on load. `dut` is the same data as GET /testing/dut/environment plus GET /testing/dut/test-config combined; `selection` is the same as GET /testing/selection; `run` is the lightweight status also returned by GET /testing/run/status (which additionally includes per-test-case results). No side effects.

item.name: List every known compliance test case

request.description: Returns the full compliance-suite catalogue, unfiltered by license — the Testing page must remain browsable for every user; license restrictions are enforced only at selection time (POST /testing/selection, 403 if a suite/test case is not permitted) and again at execution time. `suite` groups test cases (e.g. `lpc-cs`, `lpp-cs`) and is the value POST /testing/selection accepts under `suites`. `requiredConfigFields` lists, per test case, which POST /testing/dut/test-config fields it needs — the same identifiers returned in aggregate by GET /testing/required-config for the current selection.

item.description: Compliance test runner — DUT configuration, test selection, execution, and reports.

item.name: Inverter
Create a simulated Inverter entity

request.description:
Creates an Inverter (dual-role controllable system: LPC consumer + LPP producer) with an optional battery and/or PV string sub-device — see `BatteryInfo`/`PVStringInfo` and `POST /inverter/{inverterId}/battery` / `.../pvstring` for managing them afterwards.

Requires: the simulation must not be running (400). `lpcCS` and `lppCS` are both required in the body (400 if either is missing/null) — an inverter without both controllable-system configs cannot be created via this endpoint. `deviceName` must be unique across all inverters, and the (vendorCode, serialNumber, deviceModel) triple must be unique — either collision is 400. `deviceCode`, `serialNumber`, `vendor.code`, `vendor.name` and `inverterType` must also be non-empty; battery/PV numeric fields (if present) must be non-negative and `batteryInfo.initialStateOfChargeInPercent` must be 0..100 (400 with a per-field boolean map — see `validateInverterInfo` — otherwise).

`lpcEnabled`/`lppEnabled`/`cobEnabled`/`moiEnabled`/`mobEnabled` and `mpcEnabled` in the body are ignored — the server always overwrites them from the license/feature configuration, same as `brandName` (always "Coretech-Innovations") and `gridCode` (always "VDE-AR-N 4105:2018"). `lpcCS.contractualPowerMax`/`lppCS.contractualPowerMax` are also cleared before validation (not settable at creation).

item.name: Get the simulated grid connection status

request.description: Reads the same process-wide flag toggled by POST /inverter/gridToggle.

item.name: Toggle the simulated grid connection (all inverters)

request.description: Flips a single process-wide grid-connection flag shared by every inverter — not per-inverter. While disconnected ("OFF"), each simulation tick skips recomputing PV production and battery charge/discharge targets entirely for every inverter (their power output freezes at its last simulated value rather than dropping to zero), simulating an islanding/outage condition. The disconnected state is also reported to any paired HEMS/ControlBox via MOI (`InverterState.gridConnection` = "disconnected") and via a DeviceConfiguration key. There is no error path — this endpoint always succeeds.

item.name: List all inverters

request.description: One entry per inverter with its config, SKI, device address, HEMS-connection state and both controllable systems' live FSM states. Empty array if none exist.

item.name: Set the irradiance (sun) factor on every inverter's PV string

request.description: Applies `sunFactor` to every inverter's PV string in one call — for per-inverter control use `PATCH /inverter/{inverterId}/pvstring` instead. Validated up front (before iterating inverters): if no inverter has a PV string, an out-of-range value is still rejected rather than silently accepted. Inverters without a PV string are skipped (not an error). See `ValidateSunFactor`.

item.name: Update an inverter's configuration

request.description: Partial update: the current config is read, the JSON body is bound on top of it (so omitted fields keep their previous value — unlike a strict PATCH-merge, arrays/objects present in the body fully replace their old value), then re-validated with the same rules as `POST /inverter/add`. `brandName` cannot be changed (restored from the old config before comparing/applying); `lpcCS.contractualPowerMax`/`lppCS.contractualPowerMax` are cleared the same way as on creation. If the resulting config is byte-identical to the old one, the endpoint still returns 200 with `changes`/`new`/`old` but applies nothing. Device identity fields (deviceName/deviceCode/serialNumber/vendor/etc.) are only actually pushed into the running EEBUS service if the service has not started yet — see `SetNewConfiguration`; renaming a paired inverter takes effect in the API response but not on the wire until it is deleted and re-added.

item.name: Delete an inverter

header.description: Internal token used by test automation to bypass the active-test-run block.

request.description:
Tears down the inverter's EEBUS service (untrusting every paired remote first), disconnects it from the simulated grid bus, and removes it from the engine.

Requires: the simulation must not be running (400), and no compliance test run may be active unless the request carries a valid X-EEBUS-Internal-Test-Token header (409 otherwise).

item.name: Get the battery configuration and live values

request.description: 404 if the inverter itself does not exist; 400 if it exists but has no battery sub-device configured (`batteryInfo` was omitted on `POST /inverter/add`). From here on, every endpoint under this tag resolves the inverter via the shared `resolveInverter` helper, which returns 404 for both "no such inverter ID" and "ID belongs to a different entity type" — unlike the simpler GETs earlier in this tag (lpcCurrentState etc.), which use 400 for the latter case.

item.name: Update the battery configuration

request.description: Applies a partial update to the battery. Omitted fields keep their current value. Setting chargingEnabled or dischargingEnabled to false is a hard limit that overrides whatever COB, LPC or LPP would otherwise request.

item.name: Toggle the battery simulation/testing mode

request.description: Switches the battery between simulation and testing mode. Pinned values are set via PATCH /inverter/{inverterId}/battery/values. While the inverter is in testing mode the battery must stay in it: testingMode false is rejected with 409 (see lockedByParent in the response). A battery put into testing mode by this endpoint stays in it when the inverter leaves testing mode. This includes a battery that was already in testing mode because of the inverter: testingMode true makes that testing mode the battery's own.

item.name: Set the battery forced values (testing mode only)

request.description: Pins the battery's DC/MOB overrides and operating state verbatim. Requires testing mode (400 otherwise). Every field optional.

item.name: Get the inverter battery's state of charge

request.description: Thin wrapper returning just the battery's state of charge — for the full configuration and live values use `GET /inverter/{inverterId}/battery` instead. When the inverter has no battery the call is a 400 ("Battery is not available") and no state of charge is returned.

item.name: Get the inverter's AC electrical measurements

request.description: Returns the inverter's current total power, energy consumed/produced, and per-phase current/voltage — derived each simulation tick from its battery/PV sub-devices' physics (`Inverter.updateMpcData`), in the array-based `measurementData` shape (distinct from the object-keyed `MPCMeasurements` shape EVSE/HeatPump use for their own electricalMeasurements GET). Always 200; there is no error path once the ID resolves.

item.name: Manually inject electrical measurements into the inverter

request.description:
Overwrites the inverter's electrical measurements (power/current/voltage per phase, energy, frequency) for simulation/testing purposes, bypassing normal use-case computation. Requires: the simulation must be running, and no PV string or battery may currently be available on this inverter (checked via `IsBatteryOrPVStringAvailable`) — if either is available, the request is rejected so manual measurements cannot fight their own simulated behavior. Only fields present in the request body are changed; omitted fields keep their current value (the current measurement snapshot is read first and the body is bound on top of it).

Known quirk: injected values are written into the SPINE MPC local data (visible to a paired HEMS/ControlBox via `GET /hems/MpcMeasurementData` / `GET /controlbox/MpcMeasurementData`) but are **not** reflected back on the sibling `GET /inverter/{inverterId}/electricalMeasurements` — the code path that would sync them back (`h.measurements = measurements`) is commented out, the same quirk documented on `PATCH /evse/{evseId}/electricalMeasurements`. Use the HEMS/ControlBox MPC endpoint to verify an injected value took effect, not this endpoint's own GET.

item.name: Get the inverter's latest received heartbeat

request.description: The heartbeat the inverter last received from its paired HEMS/ControlBox, read from the LPC side if present, otherwise the LPP side.

item.name: Get the inverter's latest sent heartbeat

request.description: Read from the LPC controllable system's heartbeat sender if present, otherwise the LPP one (an inverter always has at least one, since both are required at creation).

item.name: Force the inverter's LPC (consumption) controllable-system state

request.description:
Inject the inverter's consumption (LPC) controllable system into a chosen state once, so a tester can start a scenario with the device already in that state. The real state machine resumes on the next tick. See `CSState` for what each of the five states means. Both `.../lpc/forceState` and `.../lpp/forceState` are generated from one shared Go route builder (`inverterForceStateRoute`), so the two roles behave identically apart from which controllable system is targeted.

Requires: the inverter must have an LPC controllable system (always true — `lpcCs` is mandatory on `POST /inverter/add`), AND the inverter must already be in testing mode (`PATCH /inverter/{inverterId}/mode` with `testingMode=true`) — both are checked, and either missing returns 400. This requirement is not currently reflected in the request/response examples of the sibling EVSE/HeatPump forceState endpoints' wording verbatim, but the underlying check (`Inverter.ForceCSState` → `!h.IsTesting()`) is identical to EVSE's. This is a one-shot injection: applied on the next simulate tick, not re-applied afterwards.

item.name: Get the Active Power Consumption Limit (APCL) currently in force on this inverter

request.description: Reads the inverter's own LPC controllable-system state directly (not a value sent by a remote HEMS/ControlBox — this is what the inverter itself currently reports/enforces). 400 if the inverter has no LPC controllable system configured ("no LPC supported") — in practice unreachable since `POST /inverter/add` requires `lpcCS`.

item.name: Get the inverter's LPC (consumption) controllable-system state

request.description: The inverter is a dual-role controllable system: this reports the consumption (LPC) side's live FSM state; see `GET .../lppCurrentState` for the production (LPP) side. See `CSState` for what each of the five values means. Note: on this route (and every other simple GET below down to electricalMeasurements), a resolved-but-wrong-type entity ID returns 400 "Failed to get inverter entity", not 404 — 404 is reserved for an ID that does not exist in the engine at all. This differs from the newer `resolveInverter`-based endpoints further down this tag (battery/pvstring/mode/values/forceState), which return 404 for both cases.

item.name: Get the inverter's configured LPC failsafe value/duration

request.description: Derived directly from the LPC controllable system's own config (failsafeValue, failsafeDuration × 3600 for seconds) — not read from a SPINE device-configuration reply. Never errors; returns a zero-value FCAPL if the inverter has no LPC controllable system.

item.name: Get the inverter's LPC (consumption) power constraints

request.description: Nominal/contractual maximum consumption power, read from the LPC controllable system's electrical-connection characteristics (same shared shape used by EVSE/HeatPump — see `EVSEPowerConstraints`). There is no equivalent `lppPowerConstraints` route for the production side — `Inverter.GetLPPCSPowerConstraints` exists in the Go code but is not wired to any REST endpoint.

item.name: Force the inverter's LPP (production) controllable-system state

request.description: Production-side counterpart of `POST /inverter/{inverterId}/lpc/forceState` — same shared handler, same rules (including the testing-mode requirement), targeting the LPP controllable system instead.

item.name: Get the Active Power Production Limit (APPL) currently in force on this inverter

request.description: Production-side counterpart of GET .../lpcActivePowerLimit. 400 if the inverter has no LPP controllable system configured ("no LPP supported") — in practice unreachable since POST /inverter/add requires lppCS.

item.name: Get the inverter's LPP (production) controllable-system state

request.description: The production-side counterpart of GET .../lpcCurrentState. See CSState for what each value means.

item.name: Get the inverter's configured LPP failsafe value/duration

request.description: Production-side counterpart of GET .../lpcFailsafeValues. Never errors; returns a zero-value FSAPPL if the inverter has no LPP controllable system.

item.name: Get the inverter AC-level simulation/testing mode and pinned values

request.description: mode is "simulation" (default, AC report derived from the battery/PV sub-devices) or "testing" (report pinned to whatever was last set via PATCH /inverter/{inverterId}/values). live always reports the currently effective readings, whichever mode is active. Distinct from the battery's and PV string's own simulation/testing mode (PATCH .../battery/mode, .../pvstring/mode), which pin their DC-side values independently.

item.name: Toggle the inverter AC-level simulation/testing mode

request.description: Switches the inverter's AC report between simulation and testing mode. The pinned override values are set separately via PATCH /inverter/{inverterId}/values. Enabling also puts the battery and PV string into testing mode if they are not in it yet (each pinned at its current power); while the inverter stays in testing mode they cannot leave it. Disabling returns the ones that are in testing mode because of the inverter to simulation mode; one put into testing mode through its own mode endpoint stays in it.

item.name: Get the PV string configuration and live values

request.description: 400 if the inverter has no PV string sub-device configured (`pvstringInfo` was omitted on POST /inverter/add). See PATCH .../pvstring/mode and .../pvstring/values for the PV string's own simulation/testing controls, independent of the inverter's own AC-level mode.

item.name: Update the PV string configuration

request.description: Applies a partial update to the PV string. Omitted fields keep their current value. Setting productionEnabled to false stops production regardless of the LPP limit.

item.name: Toggle the PV string simulation/testing mode

request.description: Switches the PV string between simulation and testing mode. Pinned values are set via PATCH /inverter/{inverterId}/pvstring/values. While the inverter is in testing mode the PV string must stay in it: testingMode false is rejected with 409 (see lockedByParent in the response). A PV string put into testing mode by this endpoint stays in it when the inverter leaves testing mode. This includes a PV string that was already in testing mode because of the inverter: testingMode true makes that testing mode the PV string's own.

item.name: Set the PV string forced values (testing mode only)

request.description: Pins the PV string's DC/extra overrides verbatim. Requires testing mode (400 otherwise). Every field optional.

item.name: Get the inverter's SHIP pairing QR code text

request.description: Returns the SHIP pairing QR code text (shipID/fingerprint/secret encoded) for this inverter's own EEBUS service. Requires the service to have already started — call `POST /inverter/{inverterId}/trust` at least once first (its first call boots the service); otherwise 400 "service not initialized".

item.name: Trust a remote device / start pairing for this inverter

request.description:
Registers `remoteSki` as trusted for SHIP pairing on this inverter. If the inverter's EEBUS service has not started yet (empty local SKI) it is started (`Run()`) first, as part of the same call, and the SKI is registered either way — so the first trust call on a freshly created inverter both boots the service and establishes the trust edge. `remoteSki` is required and normalized.

Requires: the simulation must not be in the brief transitional "stopping" window after `POST /sim` `action: stop` (`Engine.isAllowedToPairDevices` — despite its name this is **not** "the simulation must be running": it also returns true while the simulation has never been started, or is fully stopped; only the few seconds while a Stop() teardown is in flight return false). 400 "Simulation not running" otherwise (the error message is misleading given the actual condition).

item.name: Untrust a remote device from this inverter

request.description: Disconnects (if connected) and unregisters remoteSki. Does not require the simulation to be running.

item.name: Set the inverter AC-level forced measurement values (testing mode only)

request.description: Pins the inverter's AC MPC + MOI report verbatim. Requires testing mode (400 otherwise). Distinct from the battery/PV DC pins. Every field optional.

item.description: Simulated PV/battery inverter entities (LPC+LPP controllable systems, MOB/MOI monitoring).

item.name: ControlBox
Get the ControlBox

request.description: Returns the ControlBox's engine ID, configuration and local SKI, or an empty array `[]` (200, not 404) if none has been added yet — mirrors the vacuous-list convention used elsewhere in this API rather than a 404.

item.name: Update the ControlBox's image

request.description:
Despite accepting the full `ControlBoxInfo` shape as its request body, this endpoint only ever applies a change to `ImgBase64` — every other field in the body is silently ignored (bound onto a copy of the config, then discarded except for the image comparison). Behavior branches on both whether the image actually changed and whether the simulation is running:
- Image changed, simulation running → 200 `{"status":"Successfully updated the
  Image"}`.

- Image changed, simulation stopped → 200 `{"status":"OK"}`.
- Image unchanged (byte-identical to the current value, including both empty),
  simulation running → 400 `{"err":"Simulation is running, Can not update the
  CB"}`.

- Image unchanged, simulation stopped → 400 `{"err":"Invalid request body"}`.
In other words a request whose `ImgBase64` does not differ from the ControlBox's current value always fails with 400, regardless of simulation state.

item.name: Delete the ControlBox

header.description: Internal token used by test automation to bypass the active-test-run block.

request.description:
Tears down the ControlBox's EEBUS service, unregisters it from the engine, and (if one existed) always responds 200 — there is no 404 for "no ControlBox exists" on this route; deleting when none exists is a silent no-op that still returns `{"status":"OK"}`.

Requires: the simulation must not be running (400), and no compliance test run may be active unless the request carries a valid X-EEBUS-Internal-Test-Token header (409 otherwise).

item.name: Get the Active Power Consumption Limit reported by all paired LPC devices

request.description: Returns each connected LPC device's current APCL as an object keyed by device address (**not** an array — the same map-vs-array distinction as `GET /hems/ActivePowerConsumptionLimit`). Devices whose APCL could not be read are omitted. See `GET /controlbox/LpcDevicesData` for the same data alongside failsafe values and constraints.

item.name: Send the Active Power Consumption Limit (APCL) to all paired LPC devices

request.description:
ControlBox equivalent of `POST /hems/ActivePowerConsumptionLimit` — the ControlBox is the limit **sender**, commanding every downstream device paired to it and exposing the LPC controllable-system role (mirrors HEMS/EnergyGuard's own LPC sender behavior). Sends an LPC load-control limit write to every connected device (splitting `value` evenly across all of them when active=true and value > 0). `active` is required; `value` is additionally required when `active` is true (400 "Data missing" otherwise). See `lpcAPCL` for the durationSeconds/durationIndefinite precedence rule.

`success` reflects whether *all* targeted devices accepted the write — see `ControlBoxAPCLSuccessResponse` for the exact semantics. **Differs from HEMS**: when zero LPC devices are connected, this endpoint reports success=**false** (HEMS reports true for the same vacuous case) — verified against `ControlBox.SendLpcApclToAllDevices`. See `GET /controlbox/LpcDevicesData` to discover connected devices' addresses and current APCL state.

item.name: Send the Active Power Consumption Limit (APCL) to all paired LPC devices (partial)

request.description: Behaves like `POST /controlbox/ActivePowerConsumptionLimit`, except `active` is not required — the raw body is forwarded as-is (any subset of fields).

item.name: Send the Active Power Consumption Limit (APCL) to one LPC device

request.description: Same validation and semantics as `POST /controlbox/ActivePowerConsumptionLimit`, targeted at a single device. `deviceAddress` is looked up among the ControlBox's LPC controllable-system remote entities (`GET /controlbox/LpcDevicesData` lists valid addresses); an unknown address returns 404.

item.name: Send the Active Power Consumption Limit (APCL) to one LPC device (partial)

request.description: Behaves like `POST .../{deviceAddress}`, except `active` is not required — the raw body is forwarded as-is (any subset of fields).

item.name: Get Active Power Consumption Limit constraints from all paired LPC devices

request.description: Returns each connected LPC device's nominal/contractual power-consumption constraints as an object keyed by device address (not an array — the previous bare `type: array` schema did not match `ControlBox.GetLpcConstaraintsFromAllDevices`, which returns `map[string]hubapi.LpcConstraints`). Devices whose electrical connection characteristics could not be read are omitted.

item.name: Get the Active Power Production Limit reported by all paired LPP devices

request.description: Returns each connected LPP device's current APPL as an object keyed by device address (**not** an array — same map-vs-array fix as the LPC endpoints above). Devices whose APPL could not be read are omitted.

item.name: Send the Active Power Production Limit (APPL) to all paired LPP devices

request.description:
ControlBox equivalent of `POST /hems/ActivePowerProductionLimit` — the ControlBox is the limit sender for LPP too (production side), commanding every downstream device paired to it that exposes the LPP controllable-system role. Sends an LPP load-control limit write to every connected device (splitting `value` evenly across all of them when active=true and value < 0). `active` is required; `value` is additionally required when `active` is true (400 "Data missing" otherwise).

`success` reflects whether *all* targeted devices accepted the write. **Differs from HEMS**: when zero LPP devices are connected, this endpoint reports success=**false** (HEMS reports true for the same vacuous case) — verified against `ControlBox.SendLppApplToAllDevices`. See `GET /controlbox/LppDevicesData` to discover connected devices.

Requires: the LPP use case to be enabled. In practice the corresponding `useCasesEnable.LppEnabled == nil` check in the handler never fires once the server is running — that flag is set once at startup and is never left unset — so this 400 branch is not reachable in a running server; LPP availability is actually enforced by license validity (see `POST /license`, 403 responses).

item.name: Send the Active Power Production Limit (APPL) to all paired LPP devices (partial)

request.description: Behaves like the POST, except `active` is not required — the raw body is forwarded as-is (any subset of fields). Same LPP-enabled gate as the POST (not reachable once the server is running).

item.name: Send the Active Power Production Limit (APPL) to one LPP device

request.description: Same validation and semantics as `POST /controlbox/ActivePowerProductionLimit`, targeted at a single device. `deviceAddress` is looked up among the ControlBox's LPP controllable-system remote entities (`GET /controlbox/LppDevicesData` lists valid addresses).

item.name: Send the Active Power Production Limit (APPL) to one LPP device (partial)

request.description: Behaves like the POST, except `active` is not required.

item.name: Get Active Power Production Limit constraints from all paired LPP devices

request.description: Returns each connected LPP device's nominal/contractual power-production constraints as an object keyed by device address (not a bare array — the previous `type: array` schema did not match `ControlBox.GetLppConstaraintsFromAllDevices`, which returns `map[string]hubapi.LppConstraints`). Same not-reachable LPP-enabled gate as the other LPP endpoints.

item.name: Get the Failsafe Active Power Consumption Limit reported by all paired LPC devices

request.description: Returns each connected LPC device's current failsafe power limit/duration as an object keyed by device address (**not** an array — same fix as the APCL GET above). Devices whose failsafe data could not be read are omitted.

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Consumption Limit (FSCAPL) to all paired LPC devices

request.description: Sets the LPC failsafe power limit and/or minimum failsafe duration (via two separate DeviceConfiguration key writes) on every connected LPC device. `value` is required (400 "Data missing" otherwise); to set only the duration, use `POST /controlbox/FailsafeDurationForLpc` instead. `success` reports false with reason="No entities found" when no LPC devices are connected (same as HEMS's FCAPL endpoint — unlike the APCL endpoint above, which differs from HEMS on this vacuous case).

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Consumption Limit (FSCAPL) to all paired LPC devices (partial)

request.description: Behaves like the POST, except `value` is not required.

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Consumption Limit (FSCAPL) to one LPC device

request.description: Same validation and semantics as `POST /controlbox/FailsafeActivePowerLimit`, targeted at a single device.

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Consumption Limit (FSCAPL) to one LPC device (partial)

request.description: Behaves like the POST, except `value` is not required.

item.name: Get the Failsafe Active Power Production Limit reported by all paired LPP devices

request.description: Returns each connected LPP device's current failsafe power limit/duration as an object keyed by device address (**not** an array — same fix as the APPL GET above).

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Production Limit (FSPAPL) to all paired LPP devices

request.description: Sets the LPP failsafe power limit and/or minimum failsafe duration on every connected LPP device. `value` is required (400 "Data missing" otherwise); to set only the duration, use `POST /controlbox/FailsafeDurationForLpp` instead. `success` reports false with reason="No entities found" when no LPP devices are connected (same as HEMS's FSPAPL endpoint — unlike the APPL endpoint above). Same not-reachable LPP-enabled gate as the APPL endpoints.

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Production Limit (FSPAPL) to all paired LPP devices (partial)

request.description: Behaves like the POST, except `value` is not required.

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Production Limit (FSPAPL) to one LPP device

request.description: Same validation and semantics as `POST /controlbox/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit`, targeted at a single device.

item.name: Send the Failsafe Active Power Production Limit (FSPAPL) to one LPP device (partial)

request.description: Behaves like the POST, except `value` is not required. Note: unlike its bulk sibling, this route does carry the (non-reachable) LPP-enabled gate.

item.name: Send only the minimum failsafe duration for LPC to all paired devices

request.description: Equivalent to `POST /controlbox/FailsafeActivePowerLimit` but sends only `durationSeconds` (the request body is bound the same way — as an `FCAPL` — but `value` is cleared before sending, so any `value` in the request is ignored). `durationSeconds` is required (400 "Data missing" if omitted). The response is the same `ControlBoxFCAPLSuccessResponse` shape used by `POST /controlbox/FailsafeActivePowerLimit` — verified against cbApi.go, which builds an identical `{success, data api.LpcFSCAPL, reason}` struct for this route.

item.name: Send only the minimum failsafe duration for LPC to one device

request.description: Equivalent to `POST /controlbox/FailsafeActivePowerLimit/{deviceAddress}` but sends only `durationSeconds` (`value` is cleared before sending). `durationSeconds` is required (400 "Data missing" if omitted).

item.name: Send only the minimum failsafe duration for LPP to all paired devices

request.description: Equivalent to `POST /controlbox/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit` but sends only `durationSeconds` (bound as an `lppFSAPPL`; `value` is cleared before sending). `durationSeconds` is required (400 "Data missing" if omitted). The response is the same `ControlBoxFSAPPLSuccessResponse` shape used by `POST /controlbox/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit` — verified against cbApi.go, which builds an identical `{success, data api.LppFSPAPL, reason}` struct for this route. Unlike its sibling LPP endpoints, this route has no LPP-enabled gate at all in the handler (present or absent, the flag never blocks in a running server — see the APPL endpoints above).

item.name: Send only the minimum failsafe duration for LPP to one device

request.description: Equivalent to `POST /controlbox/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit/{deviceAddress}` but sends only `durationSeconds` (`value` is cleared before sending). `durationSeconds` is required (400 "Data missing" if omitted). No LPP-enabled gate on this route (same as its bulk sibling).

item.name: Get LPC data (APCL, failsafe, constraints) for all paired devices

request.description: Returns, per connected LPC controllable-system device, its address, SKI, current APCL, current failsafe consumption limit and power-consumption constraints in one call — a convenience combining what `GET /controlbox/ActivePowerConsumptionLimit`, `GET /controlbox/FailsafeActivePowerLimit` and `GET /controlbox/ActivePowerLimitConstraints` return separately. Unlike those three (which return objects keyed by device address), this returns a bare array. Does not gate on the LPC use case being licensed/enabled.

item.name: Get LPP data (APPL, failsafe, constraints) for all paired devices

request.description: Returns, per connected LPP controllable-system device, its address, SKI, current APPL, current failsafe production limit and power-production constraints in one call — a convenience combining what `GET /controlbox/ActivePowerProductionLimit`, `GET /controlbox/FailsafeActivePowerProductionLimit` and `GET /controlbox/ActivePowerProductionLimitConstraints` return separately. Unlike those three (objects keyed by device address), this returns a bare array. Same not-reachable LPP-enabled gate as the other LPP endpoints.

item.name: Get MPC measurement data from all connected monitored devices

request.description: Returns power/energy/current/voltage/frequency measurements for every connected device exposing the MPC monitored-unit role (EVSE, HeatPump, Inverter, SubMeter, compressor/immersion-heater entities) — the ControlBox's own analog of `GET /hems/MpcMeasurementData`. Requires: the MPC use case to be enabled. In practice the corresponding `useCasesEnable.MpcEnabled == nil` check in the handler never fires once the server is running — that flag is set once at startup and never left unset — so the 400 branch below is not reachable in a running server; MPC availability is actually enforced by license validity.

item.name: Create the ControlBox entity

request.description:
Creates the singleton ControlBox — a simulated EEBUS GridConnectionHub that acts as the limit **sender** to paired downstream controllable-system devices (mirroring HEMS's LPC/LPP role: see `POST /controlbox/ActivePowerConsumptionLimit` etc.) and, via MGCP, as the grid-connection-point (GCP) meter **server** a paired HEMS reads from — see `GET /hems/MgcpMeasurementData`, which stays empty until this ControlBox is added and trust-paired to that HEMS.

Requires: the simulation must not be running (400), and at most one ControlBox may exist at a time — a second POST fails with 400 "cb is already added" (the entity is a process-wide singleton; delete the existing one first via `DELETE /controlbox`).

`vendorCode`, `deviceModel`, `serialNumber` and `DeviceName` must each be non-empty (400 with a per-field `{"<field>":"Invalid"}` map otherwise); `deviceBrand` must also be non-empty to pass validation, but the value sent is discarded — the server always overwrites it with `"Coretech-Innovations"`. The LPC/MPC/LPP/MGCP use-case-enabled flags are likewise set from the server's license/feature configuration, not from the request body. `trustConnections` peers (if any) are mutually trusted once the simulation starts — see `TrustPeerRef`.

item.name: List every device connected to the ControlBox

request.description: Returns every paired remote device (real or simulated, LPC/LPP/MPC/MGCP alike), not just LPC devices — broader than `GET /controlbox/LpcDevicesData`. Each entry is keyed by SKI, not deviceAddress: verified against `ControlBox.GetConnectedNodes`, which returns `[]internal.Node` — there is no `deviceAddress` field on this type (the previous schema's `{deviceAddress, ski}` shape did not match). Returns an empty array (200) when nothing is connected.

item.name: List the ControlBox's connected real (external) devices

request.description: Returns the ControlBox's connected entities filtered down to those flagged `isExternal` (real paired devices, not simulated ones) — the ControlBox-only analog of `GET /hems/extDevices` (which additionally folds in the ControlBox's entities when one is present; this endpoint returns just the ControlBox's own). Returns an empty array `[]` (200) when there are none, not 404 — 404 is reserved for "no ControlBox exists at all".

item.name: Get the ControlBox's heartbeat sender state

request.description: Reports whether the heartbeat sender toggled by POST /controlbox/heartbeat is currently running.

item.name: Start or stop the ControlBox's heartbeat sender

request.description: `action` must be `"start"` or `"stop"` (any other value, including empty, is 400 "wrong action entered"). Controls the DeviceDiagnosis heartbeat the ControlBox sends to its paired LPC/LPP controllable-system devices — see `GET /controlbox/latestSentHeartbeat` for the current counter/timeout/timestamp, and `GET /controlbox/latestReceivedHeartbeat{,/{deviceAddress}}` for the heartbeats received back.

item.name: Get the ControlBox's image

request.description: Returns the image most recently set via POST/PATCH /controlbox/image.

item.name: Upload the ControlBox's image

request.description: Unconditionally overwrites the stored image (unlike PATCH /controlbox, which only applies a change and rejects a no-op). An empty string clears the image the same way as DELETE /controlbox/image.

item.name: Delete the ControlBox's image

request.description: Clears the stored image. Unlike every other /controlbox/image route, a missing ControlBox here is a **400** (not 404) — "Failed to get CB entity". A ControlBox that exists but has no stored image is also a 400 ("no saved image"), and nothing is written in that case.

item.name: Get the latest received heartbeat from every connected remote device

request.description: `result` is an object keyed by device address (**not** an array of `{deviceAddress, heartbeat}` entries — verified against `ControlBox.GetLatestReceivedHeartbeatForAllEntities`, which returns `map[model.AddressDeviceType]hubapi.HeartbeatData`). Devices with no received heartbeat yet are omitted. The 500 response documented by the handler's nil check is not actually reachable — the underlying map is always initialized non-nil, even when empty.

item.name: Get the latest received heartbeat from one connected device

request.description: Per-device counterpart of GET /controlbox/latestReceivedHeartbeat, scoped to a single deviceAddress.

item.name: Get the ControlBox's latest sent heartbeat

request.description: Reports the counter/timeout/timestamp of the DeviceDiagnosis heartbeat frame the ControlBox last sent to its paired LPC/LPP devices (started/stopped via POST /controlbox/heartbeat).

item.name: Actively dial out to a device via SHIP's Pairing Service

request.description:
Distinct from `POST /controlbox/trust` (which registers a SKI to accept a connection *from*): this endpoint starts an outbound SHIP pairing announcement to a specific target device, either decoded from a QR code (`qrcodeText`) or given explicitly (`forId`/`forPar`/`secret`) — see `ControlBoxPairRequest` for the exact precedence. On success, the pairing target's SKI is remembered so that once the SHIP handshake completes and the connection is trusted, it persists across the next `simulation start`.

Requires: the server's SHIP Pairing Service must be supported by the current license (400 "SHIP Pairing Service not supported" otherwise).

Note: on success the handler returns without writing any response body — the client receives a bare HTTP 200 with an empty body, not a `{"status":"OK"}` payload.

item.name: Trust a remote device (announcer pairing)

request.description:
Registers `remoteSki` as trusted so the SHIP announcer/discovery pairing flow can complete with that device. `remoteSki` is normalized (case/format) before use; empty after normalization → 400.

Requires: the simulation must not be in the brief transitional "stopping" window after `POST /sim` `action: stop` (`Engine.isAllowedToPairDevices` — despite its name this is **not** "the simulation must be running": it also returns true while the simulation has never been started, or is fully stopped; only the few seconds while a Stop() teardown is in flight return false). 400 "Simulation not running" otherwise (the error message is misleading given the actual condition) — unlike `DELETE /controlbox/trust`, which has no such requirement. Distinct from `POST /controlbox/pairRequest`: this trusts a SKI the ControlBox expects to be *discovered* (mDNS/announcer); pairRequest actively dials out to a specific device via SHIP's Pairing Service (QR code or explicit shipId/fingerprint/ secret).

item.name: Untrust a remote device

request.description: Disconnects (if connected) and unregisters `remoteSki` from the ControlBox's trusted-peer list. Unlike `POST /controlbox/trust`, this does **not** require the simulation to be running.

item.description: Simulated control box (SMGW/controllable-systems controller) sending LPC/LPP limits.

item.name: License
Get the current license's terms, expiry and capability catalogue

request.description:
Returns the raw license payload (customer, issue/expiry time) enriched with the full catalogue of simulated device kinds, use cases and non-use-case features (`devices`/`usecases`/`features`), each flagged `supported: true|false` so the UI can render locked items instead of hiding them. The `supported` flags come from `LicenseFeatureLimiter`, not the raw `allowedEntities`/`allowedUsecases` lists — a license that omits either falls back to the built-in defaults (see `internal.defaultAllowedEntities`/`defaultAllowedUsecases`), so the limiter, not the raw list, is authoritative. `valid` reflects `HubLicense.IsValid()` (signed, issued, and not expired as of the last periodic re-check).

Requires: none. Unlike every other endpoint in this specification (except `GET /version`), this route is registered outside the license middleware chain (`LicenseMiddleware`/`FeatureLicenseMiddleware`) — it is reachable even when `license.lic` is missing, invalid or expired, since a client needs it to find out *why* every other route is returning 403.

item.name: Version
Get the running build's version, build time and analyzer availability

request.description:
Returns the version tag and build timestamp injected via linker flags (`-ldflags`) at release build time. A development build (`go run`/`make run` without the release build step) reports `"N/A"` for both fields, since the linker variables are never set. `analyzerEnabled` mirrors `internal/analyzer.Enabled()` — whether the EEBUS Analyzer subsystem was compiled in and is licensed (see `eebusAnalyzerSupported` on `GET /license`); it does not depend on the version numbers.

Requires: none. Like `GET /license`, this route bypasses the license middleware entirely (`UNLICENSED_TAGS`), so it is reachable even without a valid `license.lic` — a client needs it to identify the build before it can diagnose a licensing problem.

item.name: Updates
Register this contact for a download-link email on the OTA update service

variable.description: Contact email forwarded to the upstream OTA service verbatim.
Contact name forwarded to the upstream OTA service verbatim. A literal space (as in the example) must be percent-encoded by the client.

request.description:
Forwards `email` and `name` to Coretech's external OTA/download-link service (`internal.SendRequest`, POST, no request timeout configured — subject only to the underlying TCP/OS defaults) along with fixed placeholder fields (`postion: "Developer"`, `company: "OTA Company"`, `contact: false`, `receive: false`). No local state is created or persisted by the Hub itself; this is purely a relay. The upstream URL and its `x-api-key` are compiled-in, base64-obfuscated constants (`RequestDownloadLinkURLEncoded`/`apiKeyEncoded`), not configurable at runtime. Both path segments are required non-empty strings — no further format validation (e.g. email syntax) is performed before the upstream call.

Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Get the latest version published by the OTA update service

request.description:
Calls the same external Coretech OTA service as `POST /newVersion/{email}/{name}` (GET, with a fixed `x-api-key` header; both the URL and key are compiled-in, base64-obfuscated constants) and returns the `version` string it reports. No request timeout is configured beyond the Go HTTP client / OS defaults, so a stalled upstream blocks the handler for as long as the underlying connection stays open. This is also what the Hub's internal periodic update check (`checkForNewUpdates`) polls to decide whether to emit a `newVersion Found` event over `/events_ws` — this endpoint exposes the same lookup on demand.

Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.description: Update notification registration and remote version lookup.

item.name: Trust
List the current trust topology (all mutual-trust connections)

request.description:
Returns the backend's declarative trust store — the single source of truth for which devices are configured to trust each other — annotated with each edge's live SHIP connection state. This is the imperative-vs-declarative counterpart to the per-entity trust endpoints (e.g. `POST /heatpump/{heatPumpId}/trust`, `POST /hems/trust`): those register a one-shot SKI pairing on a single already-running entity's SHIP service and require the simulation to be running; `POST/DELETE /trust` instead edit the desired topology up front (simulation may be stopped) and the engine (re)applies every stored edge automatically on each `POST /sim` (start) — see `TrustManager.ApplyAll`, called once all entity services are up. Entities discovered pairing out-of-band (e.g. a real ControlBox that auto-trusts a simulated device via the SHIP Pairing Service) are also folded into this same store (`TrustManager.RecordDiscoveredEdge`) so they persist across a Stop → Start the same way.

Requires: none beyond a valid license (default license-gated route).

item.name: Create a mutual-trust connection between two devices

request.description:
Establishes a bidirectional trust relationship between two peers (`a`/`b` in the body), each identified by exactly one of a simulated entity's engine `id` or a real device's `ski` (`TrustPeerRef` — set both or neither and the request is rejected with 400). At least one endpoint must be a simulated entity the Hub controls (two bare SKIs are rejected). The backend enforces device-role rules before recording anything:

  - a controllable device (EVSE/Inverter/HeatPump) can only be paired with a
    controller (HEMS or ControlBox), never with another controllable device;
  - two controllers may only be paired as the CEM ↔ ControlBox pair — any
    other controller/controller pair is rejected;
  - a controllable device may hold at most one controller edge at a time —
    adding a second controller edge for the same controllable silently
    displaces (removes) its previous controller edge ("newest controller
    wins"), tearing down the live SHIP registration first if the simulation
    is running.

Adding an edge that already exists is a no-op (idempotent, still 200). If the simulation is currently running the trust is applied immediately (`RegisterRemoteSKI` on every simulated endpoint); otherwise it is recorded and applied automatically on the next `POST /sim` (start). The stored topology survives simulation Stop → Start; it is only cleared by `POST /sim` with `action: reset` (`TrustManager.Clear`, called from `Engine.ResetSimulation`).

item.name: Remove a mutual-trust connection between two devices

request.description: Removes the stored edge matching the given `a`/`b` peer references (order-independent) from the trust store. If the simulation is currently running, the live SHIP registration is torn down on every simulated endpoint of the edge (`UnregisterRemoteSKI`) as part of the same call. Removing an edge that is not present is a no-op (still 200) — the response does not distinguish "removed" from "was not present".

item.description: Declarative mutual-trust topology between simulated entities and real devices (persists across simulation restarts).

item.name: Analyzer
Delete a bookmark

request.description: Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature and the analyzer storage backend to be enabled.

item.name: Switch between manual and automatic capture mode

request.description: Switches the analyzer's manual-capture mode and applies it immediately, as a side effect calling the equivalent of POST /analyzer/capture/start or /analyzer/capture/stop. Enabling manual mode (`manual: true`) stops capture so nothing is recorded — events are dropped — until the user starts it explicitly via POST /analyzer/capture/start. Disabling it (`manual: false`, the default) starts capture immediately so the live session records traffic automatically. This stored mode is independent of the momentary start/stop actions: switching to automatic mode always starts capture regardless of its previous state, and vice versa. Side effect: fires the `capture-state` SSE event (on /analyzer/stream). Requires: the analyzer subsystem to be running (503 if not) and the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Start capturing events

request.description: Enables event capture on the live session. Events are dropped — not saved to the ring buffer, SQLite, or the SSE feed at GET /analyzer/stream — for as long as capture is off, which includes the window before this endpoint is first called after startup (unless auto-capture is active; see POST /analyzer/capture/mode). No-op if already capturing. Side effect: fires the `capture-state` SSE event (on /analyzer/stream) so open UIs update without a page refresh. Requires: the analyzer subsystem to be running (503 if not — in practice unreachable once this route is mounted, since mounting itself requires it) and the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Stop capturing events

request.description: Disables event capture on the live session. Subsequent events are dropped until POST /analyzer/capture/start is called again; the session already recorded (ring buffer and SQLite rows) is preserved for analysis. Side effect: fires the `capture-state` SSE event (on /analyzer/stream). Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get analyzer capture status and live counters

request.description: Reports whether the built-in EEBUS protocol analyzer is running and capturing, plus the live session id and how many events its ring buffer currently holds. `enabled` reflects the `--analyzer` runtime flag (default on); `capturing` reflects the momentary start/stop state driven by POST /analyzer/capture/start and /analyzer/capture/stop; `manualCapture` reflects the mode set by POST /analyzer/capture/mode. `droppedTotal` counts events discarded because capture was off or a buffer was full — a non-zero, growing value indicates lost data for the live session. All fields except `enabled` are zero-valued if no pipeline has been initialised yet. Requires: this route only exists when the analyzer is mounted (see the note on the tag) and the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Import a full .eet/.jsonl/.log file as a new session

request.description: Single blocking upload: reads the whole file into a new imported session before responding, so it is only suitable for files small enough to fit comfortably in one HTTP request. For large or streamed files, use POST /analyzer/import/init followed by one or more POST /analyzer/import/append calls instead. `.eet`/`.jsonl` files are parsed as line-delimited JSON analyzer events (with the rules engine run over them and violations persisted); `.log` files are parsed as `eebus.log` SHIP traces (the format GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/export produces) and do **not** run the rules engine on import. `schemaVersion` is only present in the response for `.eet`/`.jsonl` imports. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature and the analyzer storage backend to be enabled.

item.name: Append one chunk to an in-progress chunked import

request.description: Parses `chunk` as a sequence of log lines (`format: log`, the default) or JSONL events (`format: jsonl`) and appends the results to the session created by POST /analyzer/import/init. Chunks MUST be sent serially — each call awaited before the next is sent — so sequence numbering and the session's time-origin anchor (`sessionStart`, derived from the first chunk's first timestamp) remain consistent. The rules engine runs over each appended batch and any violations are persisted immediately, for both formats (unlike the single-shot POST /analyzer/import, whose `.log` path skips this). Returns the parsed events from just this chunk so the caller can update its view incrementally without a follow-up GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/events call. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature and the analyzer storage backend to be enabled.

item.name: Start a chunked import and get its session ID

request.description: Creates an empty imported session and returns its `sessionId` immediately, before any content is uploaded, so the UI can open a session tab right away and stream content into it via one or more POST /analyzer/import/append calls. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature and the analyzer storage backend to be enabled.

item.name: List mDNS-discovered EEBUS services

request.description: Analyzer-scoped mirror of GET /testing/discoveredDUTs — same underlying mDNS scanner, same simulated-entity suppression default. `includeSimulated=true` includes the hub's own simulated actors in the results. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: List saved filter presets

request.description: Returns every saved filter preset (see POST, below), global across sessions. Returns an empty array (200), not an error, when the analyzer storage backend is disabled. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Save or overwrite a filter preset by name

request.description: Persists an arbitrary client-defined filter (`filterJson`, e.g. the query/kind/classifier/direction combination used on GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/events) under a name, so the UI can offer a one-click "load this filter" list. Upserts: saving an existing `name` again replaces its `filterJson`. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature and the analyzer storage backend to be enabled.

item.name: Delete a filter preset

request.description: Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature and the analyzer storage backend to be enabled.

item.name: List analyzer sessions

request.description: Returns the live session first (if a pipeline is running), followed by every persisted session — imported files (see POST /analyzer/import) and past live sessions — newest first, from the SQLite store. The live session is never duplicated in the persisted list. Every `id` here can be used as the `{id}` path parameter on every other /analyzer/sessions/{id}/* operation. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get SPINE binding lifecycle entries

request.description: Reconstructs SPINE binding request/response/deletion events into one entry per binding, mirroring GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/subscriptions for bindings instead of subscriptions. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: List bookmarks on a session

request.description: Returns every bookmark saved against `id` via POST to this same path. Returns an empty array (200), not an error, when the analyzer storage backend is disabled. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Create a bookmark on a session event

request.description: Pins a labeled marker to a specific event (`messageId`, the event's `id` from GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/events) so it can be found again later, e.g. from a shared filter preset or a review note. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature and the analyzer storage backend to be enabled.

item.name: Get the SHIP connection pairs observed in this session

request.description:
Returns one entry per unique SHIP connection (identified by the canonical
sorted pair of SKIs). Two local entities that are connected to each other
(e.g. an EVSE and a HEMS running in the same hub) are deduplicated into a
single row. Imported log sessions without lifecycle callbacks are also
deduplicated by their SPINE device-address pair, so mirrored A→B and B→A
frames appear as one connection. `isActive` is set when SPINE data frames
have been observed on the connection; `state` reflects lifecycle
transitions when present, and historical/imported sessions with no
lifecycle state are reported as disconnected.

Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get request/response correlation pairs with latency

request.description: Pairs each SPINE request (read/write/call) with its matching reply/result by `msgCounter`/`msgCounterRef` and reports the latency between them. Requests with no matching reply are excluded here — see GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/orphaned-requests for those. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get the device → entity → feature dependency tree

request.description: Reconstructs the SPINE device/entity/feature hierarchy observed in the session as a tree, for visualizing what a remote device actually exposed. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get Measurement / Limit / KeyValue description maps (SKI-scoped)

request.description:
Scans all descriptor list-data messages in the session and returns
label maps for measurements, load-control limits, and DeviceConfiguration
keys. All entries carry a `ski` field so ids from different remote devices
are kept distinct. Phase information (`acMeasuredPhases`) is derived from
ElectricalConnectionParameterDescriptionListData and merged onto the
corresponding measurement description. LimitDesc includes `measurementId`
to allow the client to chain limitId → measurement → phase/unit.
This endpoint is polled by the Live Events UI every 3 s. Always
returns 200 (an empty map set for an unknown or empty session) — the
incremental cache is keyed by session id and only processes events
newer than its last call. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license
feature.

item.name: Fetch a single decoded event by id

request.description: Reads from the live ring first, then falls back to the persisted analyzer store, so linked events remain available for historical sessions and for live events that have aged out of the ring buffer. Used to resolve cross-references such as a correlation pair's request/reply ids (GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/correlation) or a bookmark's `messageId`. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: List decoded SHIP/SPINE events for a session, with optional filters

query.description: Substring match on the SPINE source device address (e.g. the shortened device name portion).
Substring match on the SPINE destination device address.
When true, return the newest `limit` events (ORDER BY seq DESC then re-sorted ASC). Ignored for the live ring-buffer path.
Return only the event(s) with this exact SPINE msgCounter value. Combined with ski to avoid cross-device collisions. Used by the UI to resolve a msgCounterRef back to its originating request.
