request.description: The primary event feed behind the analyzer's Live Events view. Three read paths, chosen automatically: (1) `q` set — full-text search via SQLite FTS5, works for live or persisted sessions; (2) the target session is not the live one, or a `after`/`before` time-range filter is given — read from SQLite so events aged out of the in-memory ring are still reachable; (3) otherwise — walk the live ring buffer for lowest latency, returning the most recent `limit` matches (not the oldest). `sinceId` supports incremental polling (only events with `id` greater than it); `tail=true` (SQLite path only) returns the newest `limit` rows instead of the oldest. `msgCounter` (combined with `ski`) resolves one exact SPINE request/reply by its counter — used to jump from a `msgCounterRef` back to the message it refers to. `all=true` with no other filters bypasses the row cap entirely via a paged SQLite scan, for a complete session export. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Count events matching optional time-range and filters (no payloads returned)

query.description: Substring match on the SPINE source device address.
Substring match on the SPINE destination device address.

request.description: Same filter set as GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/events (minus pagination/search) but returns only a row count, for building UI badges/summaries without paying for payload transfer. Always reads SQLite, so results include events aged out of the live ring. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature and the analyzer storage backend to be enabled.

item.name: Download the session as an eebus.log SHIP trace file

request.description: Re-serializes the session's `ship.frame` events (skipping lifecycle, SPINE-derived, and other synthetic event kinds that have no raw-wire representation) into the tab-delimited `eebus.log` format also produced by the hub's own SHIP logger — the same format GET /analyzer/import and POST /analyzer/import/append accept for `.log` uploads, so an exported file round-trips back in. Always reads from SQLite (not the live ring) so the export is complete even for a long-running live session. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature and the analyzer storage backend to be enabled.

item.name: Get the per-device, per-use-case lifecycle checklist

request.description: Checklist view of use-case-lifecycle progress across all devices in the session — a coarser, table-oriented counterpart to GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/usecases (`AnalyzerLifecycleStep` per row). Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get heartbeat jitter metrics per device pair

request.description: Computes SPINE heartbeat interval jitter for every observed device-pair heartbeat stream in the session — a diagnostic for detecting an unstable or overloaded EEBUS peer. For a downloadable form of the same computation, see GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/metrics/export. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Download heartbeat jitter metrics as CSV

request.description: CSV rendering of the same heartbeat-jitter computation as GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/metrics, for spreadsheet analysis. Serves the cached computation when available rather than recomputing. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get requests that never received a matching reply

request.description: The complement of GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/correlation: SPINE requests whose `msgCounter` was never referenced by a later reply within the session — useful for spotting a DUT that silently drops commands. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get SPINE subscription lifecycle entries

request.description: Reconstructs SPINE subscription request/response/deletion events into one entry per subscription, for auditing which feature-to-feature subscriptions were established during the session. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get a hierarchical device/feature timeline projection

query.description: Maximum number of timeline items kept per track. Tracks over the limit are compacted into time buckets across the full session so older windows still show activity. Default 5000. Use 0 for no cap.

request.description: Projects the session's events onto per-device/per-feature tracks for the Timeline view. Results are cached per session and invalidated automatically as new events arrive (watermark-based). Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Extract a chartable timeseries for one built-in type

query.description: Which built-in extraction to run. Defaults to `measurement` when omitted.

request.description: Turns raw measurement/load-control/setpoint events into one or more labeled `series`, each a list of `dataPoints` ready to plot — the data source behind the analyzer's Charts view. `id` on each series identifies the underlying measurement/limit; `unit` and `label` are enriched from GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/descriptions where available. Built from the persisted-plus-live accumulator, so charts cover the whole session, not just the current live ring window. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: List which timeseries types have data in this session

request.description: Scans the session and reports which of the `type` values accepted by GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/timeseries (`measurement`, `loadcontrol`, `setpoint`) actually have data, so the Charts view can hide empty tabs instead of rendering a blank chart. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get detected SPINE use cases per device

request.description: Derives, per device, which SPINE use cases were observed and how far each progressed through its lifecycle steps (see `AnalyzerLifecycleStep`). Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get rule-engine violations observed in this session

request.description: Runs the analyzer's built-in rule engine's findings for the session: each violation cites the rule that flagged it (`ruleId`/`ruleTitle`) and the offending event. For a live session, findings are served from the in-memory violation ring; for a persisted/imported session, from SQLite — and if an older import predates the rules engine being wired into the import path, violations are computed on this first request and persisted so subsequent calls are fast. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Get LoadControl/Setpoint write history and effective state

request.description: Tracks every LoadControl-limit and Setpoint write observed on the control plane and folds them into each target's current effective state — useful for confirming a HEMS write actually took effect on the DUT. Built from an accumulator cache so writes that have aged out of the live ring are still reflected. Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.name: Server-Sent Events feed of new analyzer events

request.description:
NOTE: this endpoint streams and does not complete on its own. Send it interactively and cancel when done; do not include it in a Collection Runner.

Live feed of everything the analyzer captures, pushed as SSE (`text/event-stream`), for consumers that want to react to traffic as it happens rather than polling GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/events. On its own hub-side broadcaster (separate from the hub-wide GET /events stream), it emits three named events: `event` (a JSON-encoded `AnalyzerEvent`, the payload that would also show up in GET /analyzer/sessions/{id}/events), `capture-state` (fired by POST /analyzer/capture/start, /analyzer/capture/stop, and /analyzer/capture/mode, JSON `{capturing, manualCapture}`), and `session-rolled` (fired when the live session is rolled to a new one, JSON `{sessionId}`). No events are delivered while capture is stopped (see POST /analyzer/capture/start). Requires: the `eebus-analyzer` license feature.

item.description: EEBUS traffic analyzer — capture sessions, protocol events, metrics, and exports. Gated twice, independently: (1) the `--analyzer` / `EEBUS_ANALYZER` runtime flag (default on) — every /analyzer/* route below is registered only when this is true at hub startup; if the analyzer was started disabled, none of these routes exist at all and any request to them 404s at the router level. (2) the `eebus-analyzer` license feature — checked per-request on every mounted /analyzer/* handler, independently of the hub-wide license middleware used by other tags, returning 403 with an `{"error": ...}` body (not the hub-wide `{"err": ...}` shape) when not licensed.

item.name: Subscribe to the hub-wide Server-Sent Events feed

request.description:
NOTE: this endpoint streams and does not complete on its own. Send it interactively and cancel when done; do not include it in a Collection Runner.

Server-sent events (SSE) are published at this stream to all clients — the response is `text/event-stream`, an open connection the server writes to, not a single JSON body. Streams cannot be described correctly in the OpenAPI specification format. Therefore this description should be read like this:
- 'array' represents a stream and not a real array.
- The message format of Server-sent events is standardized, see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events#fields
- Every event type is identified by the property "event" which is mapped to the SSE field "event".
- The message content is described here as property "data" and mapped to the SSE field "data".
- The associated GET API is described here as property "relatedGetApi". The described GET API must be called to get the current values.
- Almost every event on this stream carries an empty `data` field ("event:name\ndata:\n\n") and exists purely to tell the client "something changed, go re-fetch" — the client is expected to call `relatedGetApi` (or the endpoint it already knows corresponds to that event name) to get the actual new state.

This is the same hub-wide stream used by the Testing and Analyzer pages for their own event names (e.g. `testingUpdate`, `testingRunStatus`, `testingLog`, `rpcServerStatusUpdate` — see the Testing tag) in addition to simulation events; the Analyzer additionally has its own dedicated stream at GET /analyzer/stream for high-volume protocol events, kept separate so it does not compete with this stream's fan-out.

Possible schemas for 'data' for the corresponding event type:
- event: CEMConfig
  data: ''
  relatedGetApi: '/hems'
- event: saveUpdate
  data: ''
  relatedGetApi: '/sim/save'

item.name: Power Limitation
Get the combined LPC/LPP view of every known device

request.description:
Returns one entry per device that participates in LPC (Limitation of Power Consumption) and/or LPP (Limitation of Power Production), covering both the devices the hub simulates and the external (real) devices it observes as Energy Guard. A device that runs both use cases appears once with both sections filled.

The controllable-system state (Init, Limited, Failsafe, ...) is only present for simulated devices: it is a hub-internal state machine that is not propagated over the EEBUS protocol and therefore cannot be known for an external device.

Changes to any of this data are announced on the event stream as the `LpcLppViewUpdate` event.

item.description: The combined LPC/LPP view across every device the hub simulates or observes.
